decision_name: HTTP endpoint for native iPad testing BLOCKS Stage 2
decision_text:
MindfulNest Stage 2 Framework Gate REQUIRES a native iPad HTTP endpoint for telemetry (GET /state, GET /screenshot via ViewShot, port 8082) so Claude can measure breathing-circle audio sync latency at p95 on real hardware. Eyeballing is not acceptable for clinical use. 

[REVISED 2026-04-17 PER KIM APPROVAL — preflight #22 revised synthesis] Library choice: react-native-http-bridge-refurbished@1.2.9 (was: react-native-http-bridge — rejected as 2022-06-26 unmaintained; @dr.pogodin/react-native-static-server@0.26.2 was Phase 0 candidate but Phase 1 verification 2026-04-17 found it is STATIC-FILE ONLY (Lighttpd mod_staticfile, no setRequestHandler), cannot serve dynamic /state JSON or runtime ViewShot /screenshot — rejected). Refurbished fork has express-like dynamic API (server.get(path, handler) + server.listen(port)), peer RN >=0.72 (we run 0.81), last published 2024-01-24. New Architecture compat must be verified post-install by inspecting iOS native source; if broken, fall back to react-native-tcp-socket@6.4.1 + custom HTTP/1.1 parser layer (~50 LOC). PLUS react-native-view-shot for /screenshot endpoint. Build separation: CUSTOM Expo config plugin (NOT a bundled plugin — verified that react-native-static-server does NOT ship one per npm registry + library issue #8). Autolinking exclusion is MANDATORY at the prebuild/pod-install layer via react-native.config.js gated on `process.env.EAS_BUILD_PROFILE !== 'production'` OR expo.autolinking.exclude in package.json. Config plugin gating is INSUFFICIENT alone. Runtime hardening: __DEV__ === true AND process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' both required before .listen() fires. Auth token rotated per launch (crypto.randomUUID, /tmp/mn-devtelemetry-token, never .env, never bundled). iproxy USB tunnel is the ONLY supported transport (no WiFi path). See DEV_TELEMETRY_AUTOLINKING_EXCLUSION_PATTERN for the canonical gating mechanism. CI gate (Layer 4): native binary scan via `eas build --profile production --local --platform ios` + `unzip -p *.ipa | strings | grep -iE '(HTTPBridge|RCTHTTPBridge|NanoHTTPD|GCDWebServer)'` — added in same PR (symbols specific to react-native-http-bridge-refurbished's underlying native HTTP server; verify final symbol list against actual installed iOS framework), NOT deferred to Blocker #15.

decision_name: Protected fields use value-based immutability via fieldUnchanged() helper
decision_text: Protected fields in firestore.rules are guarded by a fieldUnchanged(field) helper that compares request.resource.data.get(field, null) == resource.data.get(field, null). This performs deep value comparison (catches nested map mutations). The helper is called once per protected field in anyProtectedFieldChanged(). This pattern replaces the prior affectedKeys().hasAny([...]) approach which only detected top-level key changes (BS1c vulnerability). affectedKeys() is BANNED for protected-field checks project-wide. Protected fields: parentNotifiedSkills, therapistFirstCompletionNotified, inactivityNotifiedAt, linkedParent, linkedTherapist.

decision_name: Cron scheduler policy — launchd preferred over Claude scheduled-tasks for reliability-critical jobs
decision_text: For any cron/scheduled job whose reliability is institutionally important (weekly preflight audit, anything Rule 19 enforcement depends on), use macOS launchd via ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ — NOT Claude's scheduled-tasks MCP. Claude scheduled-tasks require Claude Desktop to be running at fire time; if Desktop is closed, the job silently does not fire. launchd fires regardless of which apps are running. Implementation requirements: (1) set EnvironmentVariables for PATH, LANG, LC_ALL — not inherited from shell; (2) use absolute paths, ~ is NOT expanded; (3) on macOS Sequoia+ use `launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u)` not deprecated `launchctl load`; (4) verify script is stdlib-only if using /usr/bin/python3 (CLT stub, no third-party packages); (5) RunAtLoad: false unless immediate fire desired; (6) log to absolute paths under /Users/<you>/Library/Logs/. The Claude scheduled-task backup MAY remain as a redundant secondary if the job's de-dup logic handles double-fire safely.

decision_name: WaveSpeed poll retry schedule — MAX_RETRIES=4, backoff [0,5,15,45]s, non-blocking
decision_text: Production/tools/production_server.py PollingThread uses MAX_RETRIES=4 with RETRY_BACKOFF_EXTRA_SEC=[0,5,15,45]. Backoff is stored per-option as next_attempt_at_epoch (not inline time.sleep) so polling thread is not blocked. Total worst-case wait before giving up: ~105s including POLL_CYCLE_GAP. Raising MAX_RETRIES requires extending RETRY_BACKOFF_EXTRA_SEC (assert enforces).

decision_name: Pre-fail async CDN re-check in PollingThread
decision_text: At retry counts PRE_FAIL_CDN_CHECK_AT_RETRIES={2,4}, _handle_transient_failure spawns a daemon thread that queries WaveSpeed predictions endpoint directly (fresh http.client + OP_NO_TICKET, 10s timeout). If status=completed on CDN, option is recovered automatically via _download_and_mark_completed. Runs off the poller thread so it does not block other beats. Stale "processing" responses are accepted as failure — not a free retry.

decision_name: recover_stuck_tasks.py is the sanctioned manual recovery path
decision_text: Production/tools/recover_stuck_tasks.py is the ONLY sanctioned manual-recovery path for stuck WaveSpeed tasks. Hand-editing production_state.json outside StateManager.mutate_state violates the fcntl-lock + atomic-write contract and is a Rule 19 shortcut. Safeguards: (1) idempotency via recovered_from_cdn_at skip; (2) winner-lock refuses beats with selected_option or completed options unless --force-beat; (3) spend-ledger task_id-keyed prevents double-charge. Documented in Production/RUNBOOKS/recover_stuck_wavespeed_task.md.

decision_name: BS1 — Directus prod_locks semaphore for cross-machine safety
decision_text: Production/tools/production_server.py StateManager.mutate_state and add_spend acquire a Directus-backed semaphore (collection: prod_locks, TTL=60s, heartbeat at 30s) before the fcntl.lockf local lock. Cross-machine safety is enforced: Directus unreachable → RuntimeError (fail closed) unless env var PRODUCTION_SERVER_SINGLE_MACHINE=1 set. Machine ID derived from hostname+node+uid. Reentrant: same-machine re-acquire extends TTL. Expired locks may be stolen.

decision_name: Automatic Decision Capture (CLAUDE.md Rule 20)

decision_name: Tier 1 Q1 verdict — fix poll-hang via http.client + fresh SSL per call (not auto-restart)
decision_text: When urllib in long-running process entered stuck state on WaveSpeed poll, two options were debated: (A) auto-restart watchdog + scheduled restart; (B) replace urllib with a client that creates a fresh connection + fresh SSL context per call. Kim chose B (root-cause fix) + small watchdog as defense-in-depth. Implemented via stdlib http.client.HTTPSConnection with ssl.OP_NO_TICKET + ssl.OP_NO_COMPRESSION + Connection: close + explicit conn.close in finally. No new dependencies. See _wavespeed_request in production_server.py.

decision_name: Tier 4 Q4a verdict — multi-stage stitch (per-beat finalize + scene concat)

Rejected: monolithic one-endpoint design. Rationale: resumability matters (session saw 3 silent failures in one hour); per-beat audit (Kim can preview each beat before assembly); cache-friendly (editing one beat re-finalizes only that beat). State schema extends with phase_2 block per beat.

decision_name: Pattern: gating dev-only native modules from production bundles
decision_text:
Canonical pattern for adding any dev-only native module to MindfulNest (e.g., HTTP server for Blocker #2, future screen recorder, future perf profiler). Established 2026-04-17 via Blocker #2 Phase 0 (preflight #22) after Kim's independent 4+4 review caught factual errors in initial plan.

REQUIRED LAYERS (all 5 must be present — any single layer alone is INSUFFICIENT):

Layer 1 (JS-bundle DCE — code level): Conditional `require()` inside `if (__DEV__)` block using typed-require pattern from Blocker #16: `const { ... } = require('../path') as typeof import('../path');`. Metro DCEs the require in production via __DEV__ constant folding. Verified working for any pure-JS module; INSUFFICIENT alone for native modules.

Layer 2 (build env — NODE_ENV gate): EAS preview + production profiles set `env.NODE_ENV: production`. Babel/Metro pick up production-mode constants. INSUFFICIENT alone for native modules — does not affect autolinking.

Layer 3 (autolinking exclusion — MANDATORY for native modules): Either (a) `expo.autolinking.exclude: ['<package-name>']` in package.json gated by EAS profile, OR (b) react-native.config.js with `platforms: { ios: null, android: null }` for the package, gated on `process.env.EAS_BUILD_PROFILE !== 'production'`. Without this layer, autolinking runs at prebuild/pod-install time per platform and ships the native binary regardless of JS-side gates.

Layer 4 (CI native binary scan — MANDATORY): GitHub Actions workflow runs `eas build --profile production --local --platform ios` then `unzip -p *.ipa Payload/*.app/<binary> | strings | grep -E '(<symbol1>|<symbol2>|...)'` where symbols are the native module's compiled identifiers (e.g., for Lighttpd-based static-server: lighttpd, GCDWebServer, pcre2). Job FAILS if any symbol found. This is the only end-to-end gate that verifies Layer 3 actually worked.

Layer 5 (runtime hard-assertion): Inside the dev module, before any `.listen()` or activation, assert `if (!__DEV__ || process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') return;` (or throw). Belt + suspenders against any single-layer regression.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS for any HTTP/network surface:
- Auth token rotated per app launch via crypto.randomUUID. Stored in-memory + /tmp/mn-devtelemetry-token (gitignored) for harness scrape. NEVER in .env. NEVER bundled.
- iproxy USB tunnel is the ONLY supported transport for Mac-to-iPad dev testing. No WiFi binding. Reference: `iproxy 8082 8082` forwards local Mac port → iPad USB.

FUTURE APPLICATION: any new dev-only native module must (a) cite this LD in its preflight synthesis, (b) implement all 5 layers, (c) extend Layer 4 CI workflow with its specific native symbol grep, (d) document its iproxy port in this LD.

decision_name: Pre-flight: verify any third-party library claim before naming it in a recommendation
decision_text:
Established 2026-04-17 via Blocker #2 after TWO factual-error episodes in a single Phase 0/1 cycle:

  EP1 (Phase 0): Claimed @dr.pogodin/react-native-static-server ships a bundled Expo config plugin. Kim's independent 4+4 review verified via npm registry (no `plugin` field, no app.plugin.js) and library issue #8 ('Expo — not officially supported'). Plugin does NOT exist.

  EP2 (Phase 1): Same library claimed compatible with /state + /screenshot endpoints. README verification revealed it is STATIC-FILE ONLY (Lighttpd mod_staticfile), no dynamic route handlers, no setRequestHandler API.

BOTH errors share a pattern: capability claimed without reading the source.

RULE: Before naming any third-party library/package in a Phase 0 recommendation, advocate-agent argument, or implementation plan, the proposer MUST:

  (1) WebFetch the npm registry page (npmjs.com/package/<name>) — confirm exists, version, peer deps, last publish date.

  (2) WebFetch the library's README (GitHub raw URL or homepage) — quote VERBATIM the API surface, the supported features, and any 'not supported' / caveat sections.

  (3) For native modules: confirm declared compat with the project's React Native + New Architecture version. If README is silent, mark as UNKNOWN and require post-install source inspection as a verification gate.

  (4) For features the recommendation depends on (e.g., 'has bundled config plugin', 'supports dynamic routes', 'works on iOS New Arch'): each MUST be backed by a verbatim README quote OR a cited source-file inspection. No 'should support' / 'likely works' / 'commonly handles' language.

  (5) If verification surfaces a mismatch AFTER Kim approval (as in EP2), HALT implementation BEFORE any commit/install, document the mismatch, and surface a revised proposal with concrete alternatives. Hacking around the mismatch is a Rule 19 shortcut.

ENFORCEMENT: this LD is referenced by no-shortcuts skill (additional pre-flight step) and zero-error-qa Phase 0 Step 2 (preflight summary must include 'library claims verified per LD-158' for any task naming a third-party library).

Future application: the no-shortcuts SKILL.md and zero-error-qa SKILL.md should be amended in a follow-up session to embed this check explicitly. For now, this LD is the canonical reference.

## INSTITUTIONALIZATION (DONE April 17, 2026)

Status: ACTIVE + INSTITUTIONALIZED. Both target SKILL.md files amended in terminal CLI session (preflight #25, app_activity_log #42, task_id task-1-skill-amendments-ld158-20260417):

- `.claude/skills/zero-error-qa/SKILL.md` Phase 0 Step 2 — added as NEW 4th numbered bullet (integrated into existing 3-bullet preflight summary sequence, not a trailing footer)
- `.claude/skills/no-shortcuts/SKILL.md` Decision Protocol Step 2 — added as labeled `**LD-158 cross-check (PHASE0_LIBRARY_CLAIM_VERIFICATION):**` sub-section inserted AFTER the per-error-path template but BEFORE the 'If you cannot enumerate... REJECTED' line

TRIGGER SCOPE (tightened during Phase 0 review per CRITICAL counter finding): applies if and only if the plan proposes installing a NEW third-party library/package OR makes a specific capability claim about an existing library. Does NOT apply to incidental `import` references whose claimed capabilities are not load-bearing.

AUDIT LAYER (FOLLOW-UP, not yet implemented): text-rule institutionalization is necessary but not sufficient. Required next-task scope: (1) `library_claims_verified` JSONB column on `prod_preflight_reviews`; (2) extend `weekly_preflight_audit.py` to flag rows with un-cited library names; (3) `~/.claude/settings.json` Bash PreToolUse hook for `npm install`/`yarn add`/`pnpm add` with citation reminder; (4) extend zero-error-qa Phase 7 proof table with library-claim row.

decision_name: Tier 5 consolidated fix: server-state vs HTML-snapshot divergence
decision_text:
Tier 5 closes the 'server state vs HTML file snapshot divergence' bug class that manifested as FOUR separate bugs this session (decisions 151/153/154/155 — dialogue edits ghosting back, drag-drop image reverts, lipsync button locking to Done after source changed, trim-end listener fighting user edits). Root cause pattern: server state held truth, HTML file held a stale snapshot, UI read HTML → user's edits appeared to ghost back. 

IMPLEMENTATION: (a) New module-level helper `_patch_storyboard_L_field(app, beat_id, field, value)` in production_server.py. Single source of truth for 'server wrote a new value for a field visible in storyboard HTML.' Hardened with threading.Lock (prevents HTML write race), unique-suffix tmp path (prevents cross-writer tmp clobbering), atomic os.replace, escape chain for \\, \n/\r (Phase 4 CRITICAL fix — multi-line dialogue would have killed the storyboard script), ', ", </script> (anti-breakout). (b) `_handle_beat_update_text` refactored to call the helper (field 't'). (c) `_handle_assign_image` now calls the helper for field 'i' — closes decision 154. Returns HTTP 500 + rolls back state/override on real HTML-patch errors (Phase 4 HIGH fix — was silently 200-ing). (d) `_handle_lipsync_submit` records lipsync.source_option at submit time and clears source_changed — closes decision 153. (e) `_handle_select` detects source divergence and sets lipsync.source_changed=True. Includes one-shot backfill for pre-Tier 5 completed lipsyncs. (f) `mark_done` in lipsync completion also reconciles source_changed (Phase 4 MEDIUM fix — catches the 'user changed selection while lipsync was in flight' gap). (g) `/api/lipsync/status` endpoint surfaces source_option + source_changed. (h) storyboard_v37_prod.html lipsync IIFE updated with applyCompletedButtonState shared renderer, refreshAllLipSyncButtons 10-second refresher, Re-run button UI when source_changed is true. Phase 4 MEDIUM fix: three completed-state renderers deduped into one shared helper (matches patch_lipsync_buttons.py). (i) patch_lipsync_buttons.py NEW_BLOCK updated to v3 (Tier 5) for future rebuilds. 

QA TRAIL: zero-error-qa Phase 0 preflight id=23 (approved), Phase 3 adversarial review surfaced 1 CRITICAL (newline escape), 2 HIGH (atomicity/rollback, silent-revert), 2 MEDIUM (source_changed in-flight reconcile, HTML dedup) — all addressed in Phase 4 before this decision landed. 

FILES CHANGED: Production/tools/production_server.py (added helper + refactored 3 handlers + added lipsync fields + mark_done reconcile), Production/Event_1/storyboard_v37_prod.html (added refresher + shared renderer + Re-run UI), Production/tools/patch_lipsync_buttons.py (NEW_BLOCK v3).

These 3 decisions each describe a specific bug instance; Tier 5 is the shared fix. All 3 should be marked status=closed once Kim restarts the server and verifies behavior.

decision_name: Lipsync-targeted Kling must preserve mouth geometry + micro-motion
decision_text:
DISCOVERED April 17 2026 via the 2-lever Kling regen regression. When a Kling source is over-constrained (cfg_scale > 0.5 AND prompt contains 'mouth closed, beak closed, minimal motion, static camera, head remains facing forward' or any subset), the ByteDance LipSync pipeline (LatentSync under the hood) breaks in specific, diagnosable ways: intermittent mouth stamping, visible 'double-chin' ghost contours, mouth regions bleeding past original lip zones, lipsync model 'giving up' and letting source frown through at key phrases. 

ROOT CAUSE (LatentSync paper + frame-forensic analysis of Option B vs D): LatentSync uses InsightFace landmark detection for affine alignment. Over-clamped mouth pixels = flat uniform texture → landmark jitter → misaligned mask → intermittent stamping. LatentSync's TREPA temporal-consistency loss needs per-frame motion as alignment anchor; near-zero head motion starves TREPA. Fixed rectangular mask regenerates whole mouth region from audio + surrounding context — if surrounding context is flat (no cheek/lip plane separation), regenerated mouth has no geometry to blend into.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR — any Kling clip intended for downstream ByteDance LipSync MUST preserve: (a) cfg_scale ≤ 0.5 (Rule 8 default stays authoritative for lipsync-targeted clips; cfg > 0.5 is ALLOWED only for Kling outputs that will NOT be lipsynced); (b) natural facial micro-motion (prompt MUST NOT include 'minimal motion', 'static camera', 'head facing forward', 'no head movement', 'frozen face'); (c) natural mouth rest state (Rule 8 anti-lipsync terms stay required to prevent Seedance phantom phonemes, but must appear AT MOST ONCE and NOT be reinforced with 'pressed', 'sealed', 'tight', or 'clamped'); (d) gaze control via NEGATIVE prompt ONLY ('looking up, looking away, profile view, eyes rolled up, off-axis gaze'); do NOT add positive-prompt gaze ('eyes meet camera', 'face centered', 'direct forward gaze') to lipsync-targeted clips.

DO-NOT-STACK RULE: the following CANNOT be combined on a lipsync-targeted clip: cfg > 0.5 + Rule 8 anti-lipsync prompt; positive gaze lock + motion lock; any two of {cfg bump, gaze lock, mouth lock, motion lock}.

EVIDENCE: silcomp winner (Option B, cfg=0.5, generic prompt) → clean lipsync. 2-lever attempt (Option D, cfg=0.75, stacked gaze+mouth+motion) → frozen mouth, intermittent stamping. Both used identical audio + 8.7s trim + ByteDance pipeline — only variable was prompt/cfg. Full forensic analysis at prod_activity_log id=111. SHORTCUT_RULE8_CFG_TEST_BEAT05 (id=160) hereby superseded as outcome=failed; this decision supersedes.

decision_name: Stage 3 begins with Firestore security rules + rules-unit-testing
decision_text: Before any data-model or feature implementation code in Stage 3, the following must ship: (a) firestore.rules covering three non-negotiables — therapist can read only linked patients; parent can read only linked children; child writes cannot mutate protected fields (coins, runeStates, modulesCompleted, ownedItems, and any computed progression state); (b) @firebase/rules-unit-testing suite that exercises each rule with both allowed and denied test cases; (c) both must pass before any other Stage 3 code is written. This prevents client-trust anti-patterns (client-side coin computation, client-writable progression state) from being baked into downstream code.
notes: Registered via cascade script stage3_security_rules_first_cascade.py on 2026-04-17T14:51:37.809037+00:00. Preflight row id=27.

decision_name: Canonical Firestore security ruleset + runTransaction atomic writes
decision_text: The canonical Firestore security ruleset for MindfulNest Stage 3 is Production/FIRESTORE_SECURITY_RULES_v1.md §1. It enforces three non-negotiables: (a) therapist can read only linked patients; (b) parent can read/write only linked children; (c) modules, storeItems, narrativeEvents, arcDefinitions are shared read-only to authenticated users. Subcollections under /children/{childId} inherit parent-child linkage via get(). Atomic writes (module completion, coin/rune updates, bar circles) MUST use runTransaction with serverTimestamp() as the offline-collision tiebreaker — per Production/FIRESTORE_SECURITY_RULES_v1.md §2. Client code NEVER writes protected progression fields directly (coins, modulesCompleted, runeStates, ownedItems, sessionsThisWeek, engagementStatus, domainSessionCounts); those fields are server-owned and mutated only by Cloud Functions triggered by completionLog creates. This is the ruleset that STAGE3_SECURITY_RULES_FIRST requires to ship before any data-model or feature code.
notes: Rescued 2026-04-17 from Research/FIREBASE_FIRESTORE_ARCHITECTURE_OPTIMIZATION_v1.md §6 + §10. Kim explicitly approved the rescue. Paired with STAGE3_SECURITY_RULES_FIRST (execution ordering) and PROTECTED_FIELD_IMMUTABILITY_PATTERN (LD-125, fieldUnchanged helper).

decision_name: Pre-computed therapist-summary fields via Cloud Function
decision_text: On every create under children/{childId}/completionLog/{logId}, a Cloud Function atomically updates the child document's summary fields: sessionsThisWeek (number), engagementStatus (enum: active / moderate / inactive), domainSessionCounts (map<domain,count>), and lastActivityAt (timestamp mirrored from completedAt). Updates run inside db.runTransaction. Idempotency is guarded by lastProcessedLogId on the child doc (at-least-once delivery protection). This replaces the naive 'read completionLog per child' therapist dashboard pattern, which costs 10x more at scale. Reference implementation in Production/FIRESTORE_SECURITY_RULES_v1.md §3.
notes: Rescued 2026-04-17 from Research/FIREBASE_FIRESTORE_ARCHITECTURE_OPTIMIZATION_v1.md §13. Canonical content consolidated into Production/FIRESTORE_SECURITY_RULES_v1.md alongside the rules + runTransaction pattern (rescue 1).

decision_name: TTS Approach C (single-word splicing) forbidden
decision_text: Never build Approach C (single-word splicing of variable values into universal audio). Prosody mismatch is audible — an isolated "Emma" sounds different from "Emma" spoken mid-sentence. Unacceptable quality tradeoff for a premium therapeutic product aimed at children who need to feel the voice speaks directly to them. The cost savings ($2.35/child vs $1.04/child for Approach B) do not justify the quality degradation.
notes: Rescued 2026-04-17. Hard prohibition — if any future proposal resurrects Approach C, cite this LD and close without further debate.

decision_name: Thin vendor abstraction layer with env-var swappable providers
decision_text: MindfulNest wraps each external vendor behind a thin wrapper function so the provider can be swapped via environment variable. The five wrapped vendor categories are: VIDEO_PROVIDER (default: wavespeed_kling), LIPSYNC_PROVIDER (default: wavespeed_bytedance), TTS_PROVIDER (default: elevenlabs), IMAGE_PROVIDER (default: bfl_flux_kontext), LLM_PROVIDER (default: anthropic_claude). Reference pattern: Research/TECHNICAL_PIPELINE_RESEARCH_AND_RECOMMENDATIONS_April2026.md §3. Scope is INTENTIONALLY MINIMAL — a thin wrapper + env var + fallback hook, NOT a full adapter pattern with plugin registry or feature-flag DSL. Goal: if a vendor goes down or raises prices, swap takes hours not weeks. Over-abstraction explicitly out of scope.
notes: Rescued 2026-04-17. Implementation is deferred but the pattern is locked — when any vendor wrapper code lands, it follows this shape, not a heavier adapter pattern.

decision_name: Sprite approval rubric — documented thresholds required
decision_text: Before any sprite generation begins, a documented rubric with OBJECTIVE numeric thresholds for sprite approval must exist. The rubric must cover at minimum: (a) CLIP-based consistency score vs reference anchor; (b) palette drift threshold (hex-space delta from reference palette); (c) silhouette readability at reduced scale (sprite reads cleanly at dialogue-portrait and map-sprite sizes); (d) mouth variant count per creature for lip sync (minimum 2: open / closed). This principle collapses review cycles — without objective thresholds, every sprite becomes a subjective judgment call and Kim is a bottleneck. Original numeric thresholds (CLIP >= 0.90, palette ±10%, silhouette reads at 50% scale, 2 mouth variants) were calibrated for a painterly/illustrative style. They need RECALIBRATION for Pixar-3D style before being treated as numeric specs. Source: Research/VISUAL_PIPELINE_MASTER_PLAN_v5.md Step 0.5.
notes: Rescued 2026-04-17. needs_recalibration: true — the CLIP 0.90 / palette ±10% / silhouette 50% / 2-mouth-variant numbers were calibrated for painterly 2D style and need to be re-derived for Pixar-3D. The PRINCIPLE (objective rubric required before generation) is locked now so it isn't re-debated. The NUMBERS are open until recalibrated.

decision_name: Firestore field-level restrictions via Cloud Function sanitization
decision_text: Firestore security rules cannot enforce field-level read restrictions (if a user can read a doc, they read every field). For therapist-dashboard reads that must exclude certain child-doc fields (e.g., free-text parent notes, raw completionLog entries, parent account email), MindfulNest adopts a Cloud Function sanitization pattern: therapist clients call a dedicated Cloud Function (e.g., getTherapistDashboardForChild(childId)) that reads the child doc server-side, strips therapist-forbidden fields, and returns the sanitized projection. Security rules still prevent unauthorized therapist access to the underlying doc; the Cloud Function adds the projection layer that rules cannot express. Reference: Production/FIRESTORE_SECURITY_RULES_v1.md §3 addendum.
notes: Kim-approved 2026-04-17 as part of rescue discussion (item C4). Pairs with THERAPIST_SUMMARY_CLOUD_FUNCTION_PATTERN — both live in the same Cloud Functions codebase.

decision_name: Kling start-end frame pipeline — V1 scoped to beat_05 Tessa
decision_text:
Add a new production capability: Kling v3.0 Pro image-to-video with both start_image AND end_image parameters (existing WaveSpeed endpoint, optional field), combined with FLUX Kontext (BFL API) for autonomous end-frame generation. Goal: eliminate the Kling 'settling window' + tail drift failure modes that prompt-only generation cannot reliably avoid at 10s duration. 

V1 SCOPE (this decision): tools/kling_startend_pipeline.py CLI. Takes --beat, generates end frame via FLUX Kontext from the beat's assigned start image, submits to Kling with both frames, runs silcomp-audio through ByteDance LipSync. Output writes to phase_1.options[] with source='kling_startend' provenance. TESTED ON BEAT_05 TESSA ONLY. Not promoted to beats 6-11 until Kim validates mouth geometry + motion preservation. 

V2 OUT OF SCOPE: per-creature/per-beat emotion-arc config schema in Directus; automated end-frame consistency gate (SSIM/embedding similarity); action-beat handling (pose-reference images); Luna/Benson/Ember/Bramble/Bork support (Rule 8 mouth constraints conflict with open-mouth creature states). 

RULE 8.2 COMPLIANCE: cfg_scale=0.5 preserved (no deviation), anti-lipsync negative_prompt fully intact, no positive-prompt mouth/motion/gaze lock language. The pixel-level gaze anchoring via start+end frames is a NEW class of constraint not contemplated by decision 162 — explicitly accepted as a TEST variable pending empirical validation. If beat_05 playback shows mouth freezing, intermittent stamping, or other LatentSync failure modes, this decision is closed as failed and start-end mode joins the 'do-not-stack' list in Rule 8.2. 

STATE SHAPE: new tool writes to production_state.json beats.beat_NN.phase_1.options[] as a new option. Fields: {file, status, task_id, cost, source: 'kling_startend', start_image_key, end_image_key, prompt, end_prompt, cfg_scale, duration}. Selection + lipsync pipeline downstream unchanged. 

RULE 18 TWO-WRITE: every run POSTs to prod_activity_log. RULE 20 AUTO-CAPTURE: verdict decisions (success/fail) trigger follow-up decision registration. 

CASCADE TARGETS (on success): CLAUDE.md Rule 8.3 addendum, Production/PIPELINE_BRAIN_v1.md §19, Production/governance/kling_startend_pipeline_governance.md (new), Production/MORNING_HANDOFF_2026-04-17_AM.md lesson section.

decision_name: Phase B animation — Path A crossfade between static library frames
decision_text: Phase B hand/body motion is achieved via code-driven crossfade between static library illustrations on Vosk-extracted breath cue timing (PIL + ffmpeg composition engine), NOT continuous AI video motion. REJECTED: (Path B) AI video from stills (Seedance/Kling/Runway) — blocked per prior memory, hallucinates finger articulation and lipsync on hand motion. (Path C) True frame-by-frame keyframe animation — too expensive (~$12-24 per breath cycle) and GPT Image is non-deterministic across calls, so frames would be inconsistent. Path A preserves rhythmic precision (tied to Myrrhin's voice cues) and per-transition tuning control. Procedural particle/glow overlay (reuse m1_energy_poc.mp4 particle code) adds ambient micro-motion during held beats. If Path A reads poorly against Myrrhin's voice in POC playback, upgrade path is Path C with a freelance illustrator or After Effects puppet-warp (~$200-500 one-time per arc).

decision_name: Kling start-end frame pipeline V1 — VALIDATED on beat_05 Tessa
decision_text:
On April 17, 2026 13:49 local, Kim playback-verified the Kling start-end frame pipeline V1 output for beat_05. Verdict: 'this one works, at least — it works good enough — it's not exactly perfect but I'm satisfied with it.' Output beat_05_lipsync_startend_20260417-133323.mp4 has been promoted to live as beat_05_lipsync.mp4 (prior silcomp winner preserved).

STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE:
  • Lipsync output 957 KB, +18% larger than silcomp baseline (808 KB), +33% larger than failed D (657 KB) and partial E (681 KB) / F (767 KB) experiments. Larger output = more mouth motion stamped across the clip = LatentSync had full signal throughout, which is exactly what start-end mode is designed to deliver by pinning both endpoints.
  • Pipeline completed full cycle: FLUX Kontext end frame (BFL API, ~45s) → Kling v3.0 Pro with both image + end_image (~2min) → silcomp audio + ByteDance LipSync (374s). Total cost $0.68.
  • FLUX Kontext preserved Tessa's character identity; no visible style drift through Kling interpolation.
  • Opening ('I'm sorry. I fell.') AND tail ('I should have been more careful') both lipsynced in the same clip — a first across 7 beat_05 experiments.

V1 SCOPE REMAINS: beat_05 Tessa ONLY. This validation does NOT auto-promote to beats 6-11. V2 per-creature validation required (Luna beat_02 recommended second test — wing motion + open beak behavior differs from Tessa closed-mouth). Rule 8.3 is promoted to 'validated for Tessa-like closed-mouth single-creature dialogue beats' only. General-rule promotion requires at least one additional creature validation.

IMPERFECTIONS (Kim: 'not exactly perfect'): specifics not enumerated in chat. V2+ improvements could include (a) automated FLUX Kontext similarity gate to reject style-drifted end frames, (b) per-beat end-frame prompt tuning, (c) 5s Kling test clip for end-frame pose compatibility before full 10s submit.

decision_text:
Storyboard production buttons now route to the V1 pipelines by default.

WIRING:
  • POST /api/beat/add_options → _handle_add_options (dispatcher) → routes to _handle_add_options_startend when state.beats[beat].end_frame_prompt is set + non-empty; otherwise delegates to _handle_add_options_legacy (single-image Kling, pre-decision-172 behavior preserved verbatim).

  • Event_1/storyboard_v38_prod.html — Path B patch from patch_storyboard_lipsync_as_primary.py. When a beat has a completed lipsync AND the selected option matches lipsync.source_option, the storyboard's .mn-anim-opt.selected video is swapped to the lipsync file with a '✨ with lipsync' indicator. Monkey-patches fetch() on /api/lipsync/status + /api/animate/status so the swap survives the 15s pollStatus re-render cycle. 22 base64 images verified byte-identical.

BEAT_05 CONFIGURED: end_frame_prompt set in state so Generate B+C now routes to start-end pipeline. Other beats (6-11) retain legacy path until their end_frame_prompts are populated (per-beat opt-in).

FAIL-LOUD INVARIANTS (Kim design-call 2):
  • _handle_add_options_startend returns HTTP 500 on FLUX Kontext or Kling submit failure. NO silent fallback to legacy. Operator must see the error directly and decide whether to retry, override, or clear the end_frame_prompt.
  • _handle_lipsync_submit returns HTTP 500 on silcomp or trim failure (synchronous, before any ByteDance submission). Temp files preserved on failure for debugging.

ACTIVATION: production_server.py changes merged but NOT yet running — requires restart. On restart, the server's argv storyboard-auto-detect picks up v38 automatically (see perform_server_restart). No manual swap needed.

VALIDATED PATH: beat_05 Generate B+C + Send for Lip Sync. Other beats remain on legacy until per-beat end_frame_prompts are added. Decision 177 (KLING_STARTEND_V1_VALIDATED) governs V1 scope; V2 work for other creatures is on the roadmap.

decision_name: Preview Beat audio: bypass stale AU[] base64 via server endpoint
decision_text:
BUG reported by Kim 2026-04-17 afternoon: after editing dialogue and regenerating audio via ElevenLabs, Preview Beat would play OLD and NEW audio tracks simultaneously.

ROOT CAUSE (two stacking issues):
  1. storyboard_v*.html AU[] map is build-time-baked base64 of TTS audio. When a new TTS file is written to disk via _tts_regenerate_for_beat, AU[] still has the OLD bytes embedded. Preview Beat's `new Audio(AU[audioKey])` plays stale audio.
  2. When the selected video is a lipsync clip (has baked TTS), the video element plays that audio AND the overlay cA plays its own audio — two tracks at once.

FIX:
  • Server: new GET /api/beat/audio/:beat_id endpoint streams the current on-disk TTS via _find_beat_audio. Cache-Control no-store so every play is fresh. Range-header supported.
  • Client Preview Beat: detect lipsync (video src contains 'lipsync' OR section has .mn-lipsync-indicator). If lipsync → play video with audio, no overlay. Else → mute video, overlay fresh audio from /api/beat/audio/:beat with ?t=timestamp cache-buster. Stop cleanup restores vid.muted = false.

BEHAVIOR AFTER FIX:
  - Raw Kling option selected + TTS just regenerated → overlay plays the FRESH audio (no more stale base64).
  - Lipsync option selected → video's baked audio is the canonical track; no overlay; no double-play.
  - Previous 'hear both old and new at once' bug eliminated.

ACTIVATION: server restart required.

decision_name: All external API calls use fresh-connection retry helper
decision_text:
Kim directive 2026-04-17 evening: 'save it so it always works that way from now on, for all of them, universally, all buttons in all beats.' Response to <urlopen error timeout> on Kling start-end submit during Generate B+C.

Universalized the fresh-http.client-per-attempt pattern (decision 137 + 184) across ALL external API submissions in the pipeline:
  1. Kling v3.0 Pro start-end submit (WaveSpeed)
  2. FLUX Kontext submit (BFL API)
  3. FLUX Kontext poll (BFL API)
  4. FLUX Kontext CDN download
  5. ElevenLabs TTS submit (for auto-regen + explicit Regen Audio button)

Centralized in new shared helper `tools/kling_startend_pipeline.py::robust_https_request(host, path, method, headers, body, timeout, max_retries, retry_on_status)`. Handles: fresh TLS context (OP_NO_TICKET + OP_NO_COMPRESSION), fresh http.client.HTTPSConnection per attempt, configurable timeout (default 90s for submits), exponential backoff retry (3s → 9s → 27s), retry on 5xx + network errors, fail-loud on 4xx (client errors).

UX EFFECT: buttons in the storyboard (Generate B+C, Send for Lip Sync's upstream TTS, 🎙 Regen Audio, text-edit auto-regen) all now auto-retry transient API failures instead of showing 'Failed: <urlopen error timeout>' on the first hiccup. Kim sees retries only as a longer wait (max ~60s extra on full 3-retry exhaustion).

EXCLUDED: ByteDance LipSync (lipsync_sender.py uses curl-based submission with its own robustness; not urllib-vulnerable). WaveSpeed Kling POLL (already uses fresh-connection pattern via kling_poll_fresh).

ACTIVATION: server restart.

decision_name: Option C Directus-as-UI: expanded prototype scope with falsification tests
decision_text:
SCOPE OF APPLICABILITY (Kim clarification 2026-04-17): Option C is a PATTERN decision, not a tool decision. If the prototype validates that Directus Admin + Flows + custom Vue interfaces work for the storyboard (most complex + most-used authoring surface), the same pattern ABSORBS:
- Phase A instructional demo authoring (currently scattered across phase-a-designer skill + separate tooling)
- Phase B guided meditation script editor + TTS + cue-point timeline + multi-track audio mixing
- Image cropper tool (crop manifest authoring)
- Audio producer UI (voice stem QA, breath-cycle assignment, ambient bed selection)
- Illustration library curation (watercolor + Pixar-luminous libraries) + per-illustration Rive animation authoring
- Any future production tool

Consolidation collapses Kim's current multi-custom-tool complexity (storyboard_v37_prod.html + cropper + Phase B preview + audio waveform tools + production_server.py orchestration) into ONE UI surface backed by ONE state layer. Each production surface = new Directus collection + new Flows + 1-2 custom interfaces for specialized widgets. Total addressable consolidation estimated at ~180-250 solo-founder-hours across ALL production authoring surfaces (vs ~90hrs for storyboard-only).

The prototype still tests ONE surface (storyboard on Event_2 Luna) because that surface has the hardest widgets (drag-drop image, video A/B/C compare, real Kling Flow). If drag-drop fails in Vue custom-interface land, Option C dies for ALL surfaces. If it works, the pattern extends to every surface on the list above — new rollout decisions per surface, each cheaper than the storyboard proof-of-concept.

---

ORIGINAL SCOPE (unchanged):
Before committing to Option C (~90 solo-founder-hours), run a bounded prototype that actually tests what can KILL the plan:

SCOPE (~8hr Claude + ~45min Kim, ≤$50 spend):
1. prod_storyboard_beats collection on Event_2 Luna (fields: module_id M2O, beat_number, phase A/B/C, speaker, dialogue_text, video_options O2M to prod_video_candidates, selected_option M2O, image_override file, trim_start_ms, trim_end_ms, lipsync_status enum, lipsync_output file, kim_verdict enum, kim_feedback text, status enum pending|animating|lipsyncing|approved)
2. Views: Kanban grouped by status, Table with inline edits, Detail view with inline video preview
3. Seed 33 REAL beats with real video URLs (base64 thumbnails + mp4 URLs from Event_1 clips) — NOT one dummy beat. Tests density/scroll/render.
4. Custom Interface #1: DRAG-DROP IMAGE ASSIGNMENT from gallery onto beat slot — the load-bearing widget, priority over trim slider which is a solved pattern
5. Custom Interface #2: 3-up VIDEO A/B/C COMPARE (synced scrub if possible, inline play minimum)
6. One Flow wired to REAL Kling call (not stub), tests 5-min Flow timeout + Kanban auto-refresh after webhook
7. Permissions test: create Kim-as-producer role separate from Kim-as-admin; test per-field read/write

EXIT CRITERIA — all must pass:
(a) Kim completes full beat workflow (generate → compare 3 options → drag-drop winner → trim → approve) in <5min, matching v37_prod pace
(b) Drag-drop widget survives reactive updates from Flow webhooks without losing state mid-interaction
(c) Flow webhook return triggers Kanban refresh within 10s without manual F5
(d) Kanban initial paint <3s with 33 beats on Kim's Mac
(e) Kim rates 'feels like my tool' ≥7/10 after 2hrs real work (not 30min demo)

FAIL ANY → do NOT commit Option C. Fallback tree:
- Drag-drop works but feel fails → Option D: Retool-on-top-of-Directus (~60hr, keeps Directus as DB)
- Drag-drop fails in Vue custom-interface land → Option A (auto-patch helper, 1wk)
- Flow timeout blocking → async job queue pattern required under any option

STOP CONDITIONS (hard):
- 8hr Claude wall-clock cap — stop even if incomplete
- $50 spend cap
- Migration of Event_1 production state NOT in this prototype. Event_1 beats 1-11 stay on storyboard_v37_prod.html until Option C commits AND migration happens at Event1→Event2 boundary.

AUTHORITY: Option A and Option B remain live fallbacks. This is a falsification test, not a commitment.

decision_name: COPPA parental consent: rent Kids Web Services (KWS), don't build
decision_text: MindfulNest's parental consent flow (APP-10 in inventory) uses Kids Web Services (https://www.kidswebservices.com/) — FREE, Epic Games-backed, dual Safe-Harbor certified (ESRB Privacy Certified + kidSAFE). KWS handles: verifiable parental consent via FTC-approved methods, parent portal, consent upgrades, GDPR-K, SOC 2, ParentGraph pre-verified parent network. Integration: REST API + JS widget (works in RN webview). We still BUILD: (a) orchestration glue between KWS callback → Stripe $499 checkout → child account creation, (b) Firestore-side child data sanitization (LD-171, APP-11 — KWS doesn't touch our data store), (c) DSAR deletion executor function (APP-29 — KWS routes request, we execute), (d) privacy policy + direct-notice copy, (e) app_activity_log audit trail. REJECTED: PRIVO (paid, not materially better); Stripe Identity (not COPPA-approved VPC method standalone). Source: rent-vs-build research 2026-04-17.

decision_name: Therapist commission tracking: rent Rewardful ($49-99/mo), don't build
decision_text: MindfulNest's therapist referral commission tracking (APP-19 in inventory) uses Rewardful (https://www.rewardful.com/stripe) — Stripe-native affiliate tracking. Handles: referral attribution, commission calculation, tiered payouts ($200/$225/$250/$275 lump-sum), refund reversals, 1099s (via Stripe Connect Express). Pricing: $49/mo Starter (≤$7.5K MRR cap) → $99/mo Growth (unlimited) → $149/mo Enterprise. Payouts via Stripe Connect (already planned). We still BUILD: (a) therapist signup form → Rewardful API affiliate creation, (b) display commission data in therapist dashboard (embed Rewardful portal OR call API for custom UI), (c) tier override webhook if Rewardful's % math needs fixed-dollar adjustment, (d) clawback on refunds (Rewardful handles automatically via Stripe events). REJECTED: PartnerStack (B2B-SaaS shaped, expensive), Tipalti (enterprise overkill), Refersion (ecommerce-shaped), ReferralCandy (consumer word-of-mouth not professional distributor). Source: rent-vs-build research 2026-04-17.

decision_name: COPPA right-to-delete: hybrid Firebase Extension + custom workflow

Custom Cloud Function wraps it with: parent-verification (via KWS callback per RENT_COPPA_VIA_KWS), audit log write to app_activity_log, therapist-summary scrub (LD-165), LD-171 sanitization wipe, confirmation email. decision_text: Researched: SimplePractice, TheraNest, TherapyNotes, Quenza, Twill, Sondermind, Little Otter, Brightline, Manatee, Headspace, Supabase, Appwrite, Bubble, Glide, Softr. None offer a platform where MindfulNest could live entirely — the combination of interactive fantasy narrative + ages 7-11 + COPPA-only + therapist commission distribution + TTS-personalized content delivery is unique to MindfulNest. Firebase + React Native + custom narrative runtime (APP-23 scene composer) remains the right call. Quenza (~$119/mo) is the only marginal candidate for therapist-side-only assignment UI — revisit post-launch if therapist onboarding UX becomes a bottleneck. decision_name: VPC via KWS only — all verifiable parental consent via Kids Web Services
decision_text: All verifiable parental consent (VPC) for MindfulNest is obtained exclusively through Kids Web Services (KWS) per LD-205. No custom VPC flow exists. KWS-issued parent token is the ONLY valid proof of consent; Firestore rules deny child-record creation unless parental_consent_verified=true AND parental_consent_source='kws' AND kws_parent_id present. Related files: firestore.rules, Production/lib/kws_client.py (to build), functions/onParentalConsent.ts (to build).

decision_name: No third-party PII sharing without scoped consent
decision_text: Child PII (name, age, therapist_id linkage, clinical_notes, zaps, wishing_garden entries) MAY NOT be sent to any third-party service (Anthropic Claude API, ElevenLabs, Stripe, Rewardful, KWS, etc.) without (a) KWS-verified parental consent on file AND (b) the specific service being declared in the consent flow. Cloud Functions wrap every third-party call and check the parental_consent_scope field before sending. LD-168 (TTS Approach C forbidden) is a specific instance.

decision_name: Retention: 6 months post-program-completion, auto-delete unless renewed
decision_text: Child data is retained for 6 months post-program-completion, then auto-deleted unless parent renews consent. Program completion = all 10 chapters finished OR 6 months since last session whichever comes first. Weekly Cloud Function scans for retention-expired records and triggers the right-to-delete pipeline (LD-212). Retention counter stored on the child record (retention_clock_started_at).

decision_name: Right-to-delete: Firebase extension primitive + custom COPPA workflow wrapper
decision_text: Per LD-212 RIGHT_TO_DELETE_HYBRID: firebase/delete-user-data extension is the deletion primitive; custom Cloud Function wraps it with KWS parent-verification callback + audit log + LD-165 therapist-summary scrub + confirmation email to parent. Manual Kim-invoked deletion acceptable pre-launch; must be automated before public launch.

decision_name: Zero advertising: no ad SDKs, no retargeting, no behavioral profiling
decision_text: MindfulNest contains ZERO advertising. No third-party SDKs for advertising, retargeting, or behavioral profiling (no Facebook Pixel, Google Ads, AppLovin, Unity Ads, IronSource, etc.). RN app ESLint no-restricted-imports blocks such packages per spec v2 C7-T1. APP-31 inventory row enforces absence via DevTelemetry scanner. Business model (B2C parent-pay) prohibits ads permanently.

decision_name: Audit log every child-data access with 12-month retention
decision_text: Every read/write of children/*, sessions/*, zaps/*, wishing_garden_entries/* from authenticated sessions (parent, therapist, child) writes an app_activity_log row with {user_id, role, resource_path, action, timestamp}. Sanitization layer (LD-171) strips PII from log entries. 12-month log retention.

decision_name: TLS 1.2+ minimum on all network calls; no plaintext HTTP
decision_text: All network calls from the RN app use TLS >=1.2 (iOS ATS + Android NetworkSecurityConfig). Firebase Storage signed URLs expire <=1 hour. No plaintext HTTP endpoints in production. CI checks Info.plist does not contain NSAllowsArbitraryLoads=true.

decision_name: COPPA direct notice shown before KWS VPC flow; version-controlled copy
decision_text: The parental consent onboarding flow presents the COPPA-required 'direct notice' (what data is collected, how it's used, who it's shared with, parental rights) in plain language BEFORE the KWS VPC flow is launched. Copy is version-controlled at content-lockfiles/coppa_direct_notice.md and reviewed by Kim at every arc release.

decision_name: Child record field allowlist + allowed subcollections (revised per Kim 2026-04-17)
decision_text: The children/* Firestore collection's field allowlist is: child_id, parent_id (FK, required), therapist_id (FK, scoped by consent_scope), first_name, date_of_birth (DOB; age derived at read time), gender ('boy' | 'girl' per CONTENT_BINARY_GENDER_ONLY), current_module_id, current_phase (enum: intro/phase_a/phase_b/resolution/win/decoration), current_checkpoint_id (for mid-ritual resume), voice_cache_ids (MAP keyed by module_id), consent_status, consent_scope (array of approved services), last_session_timestamp, retention_clock_started_at, created_at. EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN: last_name, school, address, phone, child email, child IP logs, device fingerprints, photo_url, chosen_guide_name (Guide Bird is permanently named 'Chipper' — not child-chosen). NOT SUPPORTED IN V1: accessibility_profile (deferred per Kim 2026-04-17). ALLOWED SUBCOLLECTIONS: zaps/*, wishing_garden_entries/*, program_state/{moduleId}, stone_unlock_events/*, clq_responses/* (CRI questionnaire — proprietary self-report framework, NOT a validated DSM instrument), gpr_entries/* (goal progress tracking), phase_checkins/* (pre/post engagement state). MindfulNest is a B2C consumer wellness product under COPPA + FTC Act + Health Breach Notification Rule; it is NOT a HIPAA Covered Entity, NOT a Business Associate. CLQ + dashboards + check-ins are normal for this product category (precedent: Calm, Happify, Wysa, Woebot, Headspace Kids).

decision_name: Every child record must have parent_id FK; orphan child records forbidden
decision_text: Every children/* Firestore record MUST have parent_id populated with a valid FK to parents/*. Firestore rules reject creation or retention of orphan child records (parent_id null or pointing to non-existent parent). Child-level queries must always flow through parent-authenticated sessions; no direct-to-child access without parent-scope authentication. therapist_id on the child record is optional-FK (child may have no therapist, or therapist may be removed without deleting child) and its access scope is gated by consent_scope array containing 'therapist_progress_view'.

decision_name: All onRequest Cloud Functions require explicit CORS allowlist + App Check enforcement
decision_text: Any Cloud Function exported as onRequest (HTTPS trigger) MUST declare: (a) explicit CORS allowlist via cors: [allowedOrigins] option — never cors:true, never unset; (b) App Check enforcement via enforceAppCheck: true in function options OR an equivalent manual check in the handler that rejects when request.app is missing; (c) an explicit unauthenticated-rejection path at handler entry. Lint rule no-restricted-syntax SHOULD be extended to flag bare onRequest({}) that does not destructure cors/enforceAppCheck options. Reason: a COPPA product with child data cannot ship HTTP endpoints reachable from arbitrary origins or arbitrary (non-app) callers; this is Rule 19 'no error paths open.' Scope: every S3-CF-* row that adds an onRequest trigger must satisfy this gate in its preflight synthesis, not at code-review time. First onRequest CF scheduled: S3-COACH-backend aiCoach callable — that row's preflight MUST cite this LD.

decision_name: Unified 4-phase plan: generalized async/sync primitives across all tiers
decision_text:
Root cause of 140 cataloged failure modes is async-without-sync at every tier. Unified plan applies one primitive — 'every async action declares a completion contract, every consumer waits on contract' — at 4 tiers:

PHASE 1 (Path A++): Mutation-tier sync. Helper function + 4 atomic endpoints + local queue + HTML L[] patcher + save-indicator pulse. Kills state-drift class (LDs 151/153/154/155). ~15 Claude hrs, ~1.5 Kim hrs.

PHASE 2 (Closure sprint): Task-tier sync. Burns through 9 Cluster A bounded bugs + builds LD-158 library-claim audit layer. ~10 Claude hrs, ~20 min Kim.

PHASE 3 (System-level sync extensions): Session-handoff contract + monthly stale-item cron + vendor-call completion contracts. ~5 Claude hrs, ~15 min Kim.

PHASE 4 (Audit-layer extensions): weekly_preflight_audit.py catches Cluster B volitional-rule violations (rigor over-applied, plan predictions wrong, false-state assertions). ~3 Claude hrs, ~10 min Kim.

TOTAL: ~33 Claude-autonomous hrs, ~2.25 Kim hrs, 3-4 weeks spread. Each phase ships via overnight autonomous Claude Code session. Phase 1 fires first, subsequent phases gated on previous phase tests green + Kim approval (one-tap via prod_approval_queue).

Supersedes LD-204 (Option C prototype — evolved into this plan). Supersedes LD-147 (already done). Path A++ (Phase 1) supersedes LD-154 via STORYBOARD_HTML_IS_RENDERED_VIEW_NOT_STATE, PATCHes LDs 151/138/153/155.

decision_name: Overnight Claude Code sessions with caffeinate + safeguards + morning report
decision_text:
All 4 phases of UNIFIED_4_PHASE_ASYNC_SYNC_DISCIPLINE execute via overnight autonomous Claude Code sessions, NOT during Kim's active hours. Mechanism: Kim opens new `claude` terminal before bed, pastes phase-specific prompt, runs `caffeinate -dims` in parallel, closes laptop lid (caffeinate keeps it awake).

Mandatory safeguards per overnight session:
1. PRE-FLIGHT BACKUP: Full tarball of Event_1 directory + production_state.json + Railway Directus pg_dump + SHA256 manifest logged to prod_activity_log BEFORE any mutation.
2. TEST-DRIVEN BUILD: Every code change accompanied by a test. Tests must pass before commit.
3. ATOMIC COMMITS: Each logical unit (schema, helper, endpoints, widget, CSS) is a separate git commit. Revertable individually.
4. FEATURE FLAG ROLLBACK: env var MINDFULNEST_WRITE_PATH=legacy flips to old path in <5 seconds. Pre-staged rollback.sh script.
5. STOP-ON-FAILURE: Any test red → stop immediately, write failure report, leave system in known-good state (old path still live).
6. MORNING REPORT: Written to MORNING_REPORT_PHASE{N}_YYYYMMDD.md at project root with: files changed, tests passed/failed, Kim-decision-needed items, rollback instructions if needed.

Kim's morning workflow: read morning report (5 min) + approve via prod_approval_queue + optional smoke test (0-30 min depending on phase). Total Kim-time across all 4 phases: ~2.25 hrs.

decision_name: Hard cap on Kim's active time for unified 4-phase plan
decision_text:
Kim's cumulative active time across Phases 1-4 MUST NOT exceed 3 hours total. Breakdown: Phase 1 (Path A++) ≤1.5 hrs (spec approval done, beat_07 smoke test ≤30 min, UX iteration ≤1 hr cumulative). Phase 2 (closure sprint) ≤20 min (morning summary review). Phase 3 (system sync extensions) ≤15 min. Phase 4 (audit layer) ≤10 min. Buffer ≤45 min.

If any phase's Kim-active time exceeds its cap, Claude MUST stop and surface to Kim before continuing. Scope creep beyond cap triggers explicit Kim approval.

This cap enforces the principle that the 4-phase plan is Claude-autonomous overnight work, NOT Kim-participatory development. Kim reviews and approves; she does not code, debug, or iterate live.

decision_name: Staging collections /zap_staging + /wishing_garden_staging visible in Firestore PITR for up to 7 days
decision_text: S3-CF-sanitize Pattern C uses staging collections (/zap_staging/{id}, /wishing_garden_staging/{id}) as the client write target; CF onDocumentCreated sanitizes and relays to canonical (/zaps/{id}, /wishing_garden_entries/{id}) then deletes the staging doc. Staging docs hold unsanitized writes (seconds to minutes typically, longer on CF failure) and Firestore Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) retains all writes for 7 days regardless of subsequent deletes. A forensic PITR export could reveal unsanitized PII within that 7-day window. Mitigating factors: (1) rules block client read on staging collections (only authoring parent can read their own writes), (2) PITR access requires project-owner-level IAM (kimhyla11 alone), (3) window is NARROW compared to canonical-doc-persists-forever patterns. Closure plan: (a) schedule a CF that purges staging docs older than 24h (near-term mitigation, 30 days post-LD), (b) switch to Firestore TTL when GA on child-data collections (eliminates PITR liability entirely — on Google roadmap 2026), (c) revisit PITR configuration to disable per-collection retention on staging-only paths when Google ships that control. Severity MEDIUM — per-collection LD-217 exposure is bounded (own-family only) and mitigations shrink the window materially.

decision_name: Silence-compression concat.txt must use absolute paths
decision_text: In production_server.py::_silcomp_audio, the concat.txt writer MUST use p.resolve() (absolute paths) for every `file` entry. ffmpeg concat demuxer resolves relative entries relative to the concat.txt directory, NOT the process cwd — this caused doubled-path ENOENT failures (exit 254) on any beat with a silence >1.0s. Reproduced on beat_08 (line_08_guide_bird.mp3, 1.042s silence). Any future code that emits ffmpeg concat lists anywhere in the codebase must follow this rule.
past_failure_prevented: April 18 2026: every silcomp call for beats with silences >1.0s silently failed with exit 254 because the concat.txt writer used bare Path objects (relative). Bug shipped unnoticed because beats without long silences bypass the writer entirely (early-return "no_silences_over_threshold"). Related to LD-162 (LIPSYNC_SOURCE_MUST_PRESERVE_MOUTH_MOTION) — silcomp is the pre-lipsync §8.4 pattern; if silcomp fails, LatentSync starves on long silences and produces ghost-mouth artifacts, re-triggering the exact class of failure §8.2/§8.4 were designed to prevent.
notes: Locked 2026-04-18. Preflight: tier0a-silcomp-fix-20260418. Fix: production_server.py line 1449-1456 (was 1449-1452). Related: LD-162. One-line patch: `for p in scratch` -> `p.resolve() for p in scratch` inside the concat.txt writer.

decision_name: Suppress BrokenPipe/ConnectionReset tracebacks in production_server.py socket writes
decision_text:
In Production/tools/production_server.py, the socket-write paths in _serve_asset (range response), _send_json, _send_bytes, and _serve_beat_audio (range response) MUST wrap the end_headers()+wfile.write() calls in a try/except that catches ONLY BrokenPipeError and ConnectionResetError — never the general Exception class. On catch: emit a single short stderr line (e.g., 'asset stream canceled by client: {filename}') and return. do_GET also catches these two specific exceptions at the top level as defense-in-depth; the general Exception handler (HTTP 500 + traceback.print_exc) is preserved below for all other unexpected errors.

RATIONALE: Chrome cancels preloaded <video> range requests aggressively when the <video> element has not been .play()'d or has scrolled out of view. Each cancel produced a 20-40 line traceback in /tmp/production_server.log. Audit showed 4,023 of 5,366 error lines (75%) came from this single non-issue, drowning real errors. These two exceptions are strictly socket-level sentinels with no application semantics; swallowing them is the stdlib-documented remediation.

DO NOT: (a) broaden the catch to OSError or Exception; (b) silence the log entirely — one line per cancel is still valuable for debugging; (c) skip the defense-in-depth catch in do_GET (a cascading BrokenPipe in the 500-response path was one of the observed failure modes).
past_failure_prevented: 75% of server log noise was client-cancel tracebacks. On April 18 2026 a single ~500ms curl-cancel against /asset/ produced 48 log lines of nested BrokenPipeError tracebacks, including a secondary cascade where the 500-response end_headers() call itself broke. This rule exists so future refactors preserve the narrow try/except and don't regress the log to the pre-fix state.
notes: Registered alongside preflight task tier0b-brokenpipe-hygiene-20260418 (preflight id=64). Validated via /tmp/test_brokenpipe_patch.py — 4/4 isolated tests pass (both exception types on both helper methods).

decision_name: Email verification hard gate deferred — KWS VPC (LD-216) is the real adult-consent gate

The actual COPPA parental-consent gate is KWS verifiable parental consent per LD-216 COPPA_VPC_VIA_KWS_ONLY, which runs in S3-AUTH-consent. Until KWS ships, writes to child-data paths are blocked by rules requiring /parents/{uid}.consent_status == 'verified' (LD-216). Consider adding emailVerified as a defense-in-depth belt-and-braces UX check (deliverable email + unblocks password-reset) separate from security boundary.

decision_name: Server-side 60s per-beat TTS auto-regen debounce
decision_text: Contenteditable dialogue blur fires frequently as Kim types; each save triggered a ~5-8s ElevenLabs v3 TTS render (~$0.02). Without a debounce, a typing session can burn dozens of renders and dollars. Tier 1A (April 18 2026) adds a 60-second sliding window keyed per beat_id inside _handle_beat_update_text. Within the window, TTS regen is skipped with reason='debounced' while the text save still completes. Outside the window, regen proceeds and the window resets. Scope: AUTO-regen only. The explicit 'Regen Audio' button (/api/beat/regenerate_audio, handler _handle_beat_regenerate_audio) is user-initiated opt-in and is NOT debounced. The existing skip_tts_regen body flag remains a client-side force-skip (checked first, short-circuits before debounce). Failures (e.g. ElevenLabs down) still mark the debounce window so retries don't stampede. Rollback: set MINDFULNEST_T1_ENABLED=0 to revert.
past_failure_prevented: Typing stampede that would fire ElevenLabs v3 per keystroke blur (~$0.02/call, 5-8s latency). Also protects against retry stampede when ElevenLabs returns 5xx.
notes: Preflight review id=65 authorized Tier 1A. Companion LD: V2_DIALOGUE_EXPLICIT_FIELD_FORWARDING_WITH_ALLOWLIST.

decision_name: v2 dialogue -> legacy handler forwarding uses explicit field allowlist
decision_text: /api/v2/beat/<id>/patch with field='dialogue' delegates to the legacy _handle_beat_update_text handler to preserve LD-181 TTS_AUTO_REGEN_ON_TEXT_EDIT semantics. Before Tier 1A the delegation composed the legacy body as a hardcoded {'beat', 'text'} pair, dropping any client flags. Tier 1A adds an explicit allowlist tuple _FORWARDED_V2_DIALOGUE_FIELDS in production_server.py (currently: 'skip_tts_regen'). Only listed fields are copied from the v2 body into the legacy body. New opt-out flags must be added to the allowlist explicitly. NO silent passthrough of arbitrary client fields (defense-in-depth). Gated on MINDFULNEST_T1_ENABLED.
past_failure_prevented: A v2 client opt-out (skip_tts_regen=True) was silently discarded during legacy delegation; ElevenLabs would fire even when the client explicitly asked to skip.

decision_name: Per-vendor wall-clock timeout flips polling options to failed
decision_text: Production server polling loop adds wall-clock timeout check in _pending_tasks. Options exceeding STALE_TIMEOUT_SEC[source] (Kling/kling_startend/seedance=900s, bytedance_lipsync/latentsync=300s, elevenlabs_tts=60s, default=900s) are handed to _mark_stale_timeout_with_artifact_check which flips to failed with reason=stale_timeout when no on-disk artifact exists. Thresholds = 3x documented p99 per vendor. Feature flag MINDFULNEST_T1_ENABLED=0 or MINDFULNEST_WRITE_PATH=legacy disables. Tier 1B (April 18 2026).

decision_name: Stale option recovers to succeeded_late when output file exists on disk
decision_text: Before flipping a stale polling option to failed, _mark_stale_timeout_with_artifact_check inspects the expected output path (e.g. beat_NN_option_N.mp4). If the file exists with mtime strictly greater than submitted_at_epoch, the option is marked status=succeeded_late with resurrected=true and stale_timeout_recovered=true; phase_1 rollup treats succeeded_late as terminal-success. This handles lost-vendor-callback scenarios where the work actually completed but we never heard back. Strict > mtime check prevents stale prior-run artifacts from being claimed. Tier 1B (April 18 2026).

decision_name: _download_and_mark_completed never silently clobbers a failed option
decision_text: Inside StateManager.mutate_state, _download_and_mark_completed now inspects prior option status before transitioning to completed. If prior=failed (T1 stale-timeout flipped it), the option is resurrected with resurrected_from='failed', last_error cleared, and status='completed'. If prior=succeeded_late (T1 already recovered via artifact check), status promotes to 'completed' with resurrected_from='succeeded_late' preserving earlier recovery provenance. All branches go through one atomic mutate_state call. Activity log captures late_success_resurrected_{failed,succeeded_late} via _t1_directus_log on daemon thread. Tier 1B (April 18 2026).

decision_name: CLAUDE.md global pruning deferred post-Stage-3-ship (EXPLICIT NEGATIVE DECISION)
decision_text: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE DECISION: CLAUDE.md will NOT be pruned from current ~8000 words to a ~2000-word target during Stage 3. Rationale: (1) Empirical evidence — Stage 3 Waves A-D shipped successfully (23 LDs, 14 preflights, 5 rows merged, 80/80 + 119/119 tests passing) with CLAUDE.md at current length; (2) Historical failures (April 13 storyboard scramble, March 24 v2 overwrite) were decision/edge-case errors, not context-rot errors; (3) 6 CRITICAL preflight-bypass blockers are volitional (Phase 0 skipped), not rot-caused; (4) Non-engineer context argues for MORE governance text, not less, to compensate for missing engineering instinct. OPPORTUNISTIC exception: when editing CLAUDE.md for other reasons, may migrate terminology table, voice architecture, and business-model paragraph to Directus pointers. Re-evaluate as T3 polish-class item per STAGE3_EXECUTION_PLAN_v2.md section 4B after Stage 3 ships.

decision_name: Production/tools/ remains in Dropbox — no git repo migration (EXPLICIT NEGATIVE DECISION)
decision_text: EXPLICIT NEGATIVE DECISION: Production/tools/ (build_storyboard.py, kling_startend_pipeline.py, lipsync_sender.py, audio mix assembler, Directus registration helper) will NOT be migrated out of Dropbox to a standalone git repo. Rationale: (1) Four backup layers already protect this code — Dropbox version history, Time Machine, daily_backup.sh via launchd (WA-C15), weekly_directus_snapshot.py; (2) Production/tools is pipeline-ops-shaped with output-visible review (Kim reviews every audio mix, storyboard, video) — silent regressions do not survive review; (3) Symlink-into-Dropbox architectures are documented minefield (git tracks symlinks as path strings, Dropbox xattrs corrupt .git/index); (4) Full-migration alternative is ~4 hours for marginal benefit. Pytest tests (see PIPELINE_PYTEST_3_CRITICAL_SCRIPTS) are the actual safety net against regression and work identically in Dropbox. Revisit only if a specific script becomes high-churn (10 or more structural changes per month).

decision_name: Tier 3 v2 patch_state whitelist extensions: pause_after_ms, speaker, display_order
decision_text: The v2 field whitelist (_V2_ALLOWED_FIELDS in production_server.py) is extended to accept three new fields: (1) pause_after_ms — int in [0, 10000], stored at beats[bid].phase_1.pause_after_ms; (2) speaker — non-empty string, stored at beats[bid].phase_1.speaker, side-effect sets phase_1.speaker_mismatch=True so the stale-audio badge renders (auto-cleared on the next successful regen via _tier1a_mark_regen_fired(app=..., regen_ok=True)); (3) display_order — top-level state key, a list[str] of existing beat_ids, routed through /api/v2/beat/__global__/patch using a sentinel beat_id. Per-beat fields are rejected on __global__ and display_order is rejected on any real beat_id. All new logic gated on _t1_enabled()/MINDFULNEST_T1_ENABLED so rollback is one env var. Sidecar projection (_write_sidecar_L_json) updated to expose pause_after_ms/speaker/speaker_mismatch per beat and top-level display_order under __meta__.

decision_name: New endpoint: POST /api/v2/beat/create
decision_text: Adds POST /api/v2/beat/create to production_server.py. Body: {insert_after: beat_id | null, mutation_id: uuid?}. Behavior: computes next beat_NN from max existing beat_NN + 1 (zero-padded to 2 digits, widened on collision); writes a minimum scaffold (text='', phase_1={status:'pending', options:[]}, _version=0, created_at=ISO); updates state.display_order (initializing from sorted existing beat_ids if absent), inserting after insert_after or appending; mutate_state() provides atomic lock+write; sidecar .L.json is refreshed post-mutation. Idempotency via shared _PATCH_STATE_DEDUP LRU cache - duplicate mutation_id returns {status:dedup} without creating a second beat. Gated on _t1_enabled() AND MINDFULNEST_WRITE_PATH != 'legacy'.

decision_name: Tier 3 client-side widget wiring — 6 widgets atomic patch (v38 storyboard)
decision_text: Six client-side widgets in storyboard_v38_prod.html are wired through the existing Phase 1.5 _pathappWire.routedPatch() convention to persist user edits to the server via v2 patch_state: (W1) pause slider — ps.onchange (release only) converts seconds to ms and routes pause_after_ms; ps.oninput is preserved for live preview (no server write on drag). (W2) image dropdown — is2.onchange routes image_override BEFORE calling render(); matches pre-existing drag-drop idiom. (W3) speaker dropdown — sl.onchange routes speaker BEFORE render(); server-side side-effect sets speaker_mismatch=True which the UI surfaces as an audio-stale-badge (LD-256). (W4) row reorder ▲▼ — mv() emits display_order (list of beat_ids) to the __global__ sentinel after the swap. Hydrate path (_t3ApplyDisplayOrder) reorders L[] from sidecar display_order BEFORE render on load. (W5) + Add Line — addLine() now POSTs to /api/v2/beat/create with insert_after=last L[].a (or null), uses server-returned beat_id as anchor, pushes L[] entry only on 200; 503 triggers red-toast refusal. (W6) [pause] tag button — after inserting "[pause]", the click handler sets _t3PauseBlurPending=true and dispatches a blur event; a thin wrapper around window.pathappPatch forwards {skip_tts_regen: true} to server on dialogue saves triggered by pause-tag clicks. All six widgets pass a _t3LegacyRefuse-bound legacyFn to routedPatch — red pathappToast on 503/network failure; no silent client-only mutation anywhere (LD-259). Feature-flagged via window.TIER3_ENABLED (mirrors server MINDFULNEST_T1_ENABLED). Rule 7 Path B enforced: patch_v38_tier3_widgets.py reads HTML into memory, applies string replacements to <script>/<style> only, asserts SHA256 byte-identical sorted concatenation of all data:image base64 URIs pre/post, backs up to .bak_tier3_widgets_<UTC_TS>, runs node --check on concatenated script bodies, runs 11 static presence checks. 12 new unit tests (test_tier3_html_patch.py) + all 22 pre-existing tests (T1A, T1B, Phase 1) pass.

decision_name: Tier 3 stale-audio badge CSS + render guard
decision_text: A new CSS class .audio-stale-badge { color:#f39c12; font-size:10px; margin-left:4px; font-weight:600; } is injected into the Phase 1.5 <style> block. The render() function appends a <span class="audio-stale-badge"> reading "⚠ audio stale (click Regen Audio)" to the transport line (tp) whenever l.speaker_mismatch is truthy — server sets this flag on speaker-field v2 patches (LD-241) and clears it on the next successful TTS regen. Tooltip: "Speaker changed after TTS was generated. Click Regen Audio to refresh." This is a visual affordance only; no state is mutated by the badge itself.

decision_name: Arc 1 coin/stone reward amounts hardcoded in CF code; Firestore /config migration deferred
decision_text: S3-CF-coin-txn v1 stores Arc 1 module reward amounts (coins per phase_a, phase_b, completion; stone-domain mapping) as TypeScript constants in functions/src/config/moduleRewards.ts. Tuning amounts requires a CF redeploy (~3 min cold-start). This is a shortcut per Rule 19 — chosen over a Firestore /config/module_rewards collection (Counter 1 CRITICAL #2 raised real concern about economy-tuning friction). Rationale: (1) Arc 1 is 6 modules × 3 phases = 18 entries that won't change mid-Arc; (2) Firestore /config path needs rules v8, cache invalidation, deploy-ordering during seed — net-new infra; (3) v1 is data-validation scope, not live-tuning. Closure plan: migrate to /config/module_rewards/{moduleId} when any of (a) Kim tunes amounts more than twice, (b) Arc 2 begins (opportunity for non-deploy content changes), (c) A/B testing on rewards becomes scope. Severity MEDIUM — no correctness risk, only velocity-of-tuning risk.
notes: Migration trigger: 3x Kim-tunes OR Arc 2 start OR A/B testing.

decision_name: Audit writes stay best-effort v1; compliance-grade retry queue deferred
decision_text: S3-POLISH-audit v1 retains fire-and-forget semantics for post-transaction audit writes (writeAudit(ctx={db}, event) uses db.collection('audit_logs').add(...) with no retry on network failure). In-transaction audit writes (writeAudit(ctx={txn}, event) via txn.create) remain atomic with their triggering op. The gap: a post-txn audit write failure produces an un-audited Firestore action, which is a LD-221 compliance hole under strict reading. Rationale for deferring: (a) all current CF audit callsites that handle critical child-data ops (coin-txn, sanitize) use in-txn variant — atomicity already guaranteed; (b) only therapist-summary + auth CFs use post-txn variant, and their audit-loss blast radius is low; (c) full retry queue requires Firestore-backed outbox + scheduled CF drainer + dead-letter handling = multi-day work with its own Phase 0. Closure plan: S3-POLISH-audit-retry follow-up row scoping outbox + drainer + DLQ before first external beta user. Severity MEDIUM.
notes: Closure: before external beta user onboarding.

decision_name: RN component test infra (jest-expo + react-native-testing-library) deferred
decision_text: S3-ANIM-video-loops v1 ships VideoLoopPlayer with no unit tests. Rationale: RN component test infra requires jest-expo + @testing-library/react-native + jest.config.js + test setup — full-row scope beyond this component-wrapper row. Coverage gap: Maestro Tier-1 is launch-only (home screen only), doesn't exercise the dev video-test screen. Risk: VideoLoopPlayer regressions caught only at manual test time. Closure plan: S3-TEST-rn-component-setup row adds the test infra + backfills tests for VideoLoopPlayer + any future RN components. Must close before first external beta user. Severity MEDIUM.

decision_name: Lipsync honors storyboard trim window
decision_text:
Lipsync pipeline honors phase_1.trim_start and phase_1.trim_end when trimming source video for ByteDance LipSync submission.

Signature: _trim_video_to_audio(source, dst, audio_dur, *, trim_start=0.0, trim_end=None) -> (dst, actual, ts_used, te_used). Passes ffmpeg `-ss <trim_start>` BEFORE `-i` (input-side seek — frame-accurate because `-c:v libx264 -preset fast -crf 18` re-encodes every frame; switching to `-c copy` would break this invariant).

Duration formula: actual = min(audio_duration + 0.4s tailroom, trim_end - trim_start, raw_dur - trim_start).

Backward compat: omitting trim kwargs reproduces the old 'trim from frame 0' behavior (effective_end collapses to raw_dur). Verified: raw_dur=10 audio=5.2 -> old actual=5.6; new with defaults=5.6.

Fail-loud HTTP 400 conditions:
  - trim_start >= raw_dur (clip shorter than seek point)
  - trim_end <= trim_start (zero/inverted window)
  - audio + 0.4s tailroom > (trim_end - trim_start) (window too small for audio — response body includes audio_duration_s, tailroom_s, needed_s, trim_window_s, trim_start, trim_end, and a 'hint' field).
trim_end > raw_dur + 0.05 is silently clamped with a WARN log (accommodates UI rounding).

Retry state reset: when init_lipsync finds existing beat.lipsync dict with status in {submitting, polling, failed, completed}, it clears task_id, submitted_at, submitted_at_epoch; increments retries; appends prior task_id to superseded_task_ids[] (dedup'd) for audit. First-time submissions (lipsync missing or None) preserve retries=0 and do not touch stale fields.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOR CHANGE: beats currently on disk with completed lipsync AND non-zero phase_1.trim_start will produce DIFFERENT lipsync output on retry vs the file on disk. As of 2026-04-18, affected beats are beat_09 (trim_start=1.4) and beat_10 (trim_start=0.3). The prior behavior silently ignored Kim's trim values; this fix honors them.

decision_name: Firebase App Check SDK install + wiring deferred
decision_text: S3-AUTH-firebase-app v1 ships without Firebase App Check SDK wired in the RN client. Preflight 66 synthesis picked Firebase JS SDK (not @react-native-firebase/*) for the auth path; App Check via JS SDK on RN requires either ReCaptchaV3Provider (web) OR a custom DeviceCheck/Play Integrity provider (not yet scoped). Advocate 4's proposal to use @react-native-firebase/app-check contradicts the JS SDK architecture and would force expo prebuild + bare workflow migration = multi-day rework. Defer ENTIRELY to S3-POLISH-appcheck with these closure items: (a) decide JS-SDK-compatible App Check provider; (b) install SDK; (c) wire token attestation; (d) flip enforceAppCheck:true on onCall CFs per LD-229; (e) DeviceCheck iOS + Play Integrity Android console provisioning. Severity MEDIUM (bounded risk during dev — CFs use enforceAppCheck:false today).

decision_name: Firebase Auth in-memory persistence v1 — users sign out on reload
decision_text: Firebase JS SDK v10+ removed the public getReactNativePersistence API, and v12 deleted the firebase/auth/react-native subpath entirely. Without it, getAuth() in React Native yields in-memory persistence only — signed-in users are logged out on every app reload/background-kill. S3-AUTH-firebase-app v1 ships this limitation to move forward; closure options to evaluate in S3-AUTH-persistence follow-up row: (A) migrate the auth layer to @react-native-firebase/auth (requires expo prebuild + bare workflow — contradicts preflight 66 JS SDK architecture); (B) implement a custom AsyncStorage persistence adapter wrapping the (private) internal Firebase auth persistence interface — fragile across Firebase releases; (C) pin firebase <= 10.6 where getReactNativePersistence was still exported (legacy, un-patched). None is clean. Severity MEDIUM for v1 dev — HIGH for production user experience. Must close before external beta.
