decision_name: App rendering architecture: single-MP4 atomic playback per module/event
decision_text: Every narrative playable asset in the MindfulNest app (modules, narrative events between modules, Opening Storybook / Event 0, arc intros, arc completion celebrations, win celebrations, map-return scenes) SHIPS as a single pre-stitched MP4 file with all audio + video + on-screen animations + cue timing baked in at production time. Playback uses one expo-video instance playing one file. Forbidden: multi-file playlist sequencing, runtime composition, expo-audio in the module playback path, runtime audio/video mixing, React Native Skia in hot playback path. The production pipeline (Kim-side) produces each deliverable via ffmpeg/LipSync/Kling and gates on QuickTime review. This decision closes the open-bug surface documented by expo/expo issues #34050, #34162, #36034, #38671, #42595, #43102 and react-native-video #1785/#4844 decode/crash classes. See SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md and APP_ARCHITECTURE_MASTER_v1.md.

decision_name: No runtime TTS personalization in the app; ElevenLabs stays in production pipeline only
decision_text: The MindfulNest app ships ZERO runtime text-to-speech. ElevenLabs exists only in Kim's production pipeline to generate pre-rendered audio that is baked into the single-MP4-atomic deliverables. No app-side ElevenLabs SDK, no runtime audio generation, no per-child audio caching, no audio-side substitution of {childName}/{therapistName}/{parentTitle}/{parentName}/{chosenGuideName}/{childPronoun*}/{parentPronoun*}/{therapistPronoun*}. Text-UI personalization (home screen text, progress pages, AI Parent Coach chat output, email/push copy) is explicitly IN SCOPE and retained — only SPOKEN audio personalization is dropped. This supersedes LD-279, LD-275, LD-166, LD-167, and restates LD-54 as text-side only. See APP_ARCHITECTURE_MASTER_v1.md.

decision_name: Catalog delivered arc-at-a-time; M1 bundled with install; background fetch on arc unlock
decision_text:
Initial App Store install bundles: JS + Expo runtime + shared character library (WebP q80 long-edge ≤1280px) + shared audio library + Opening Storybook + M1 (first module of Arc 1). Target total ≤ 185 MB, hard ceiling 200 MB to stay inside iOS cellular install cap. Remaining Arc 1 modules and narrative events download in background on first launch. Arcs 2-9 auto-download in background on the arc-completion celebration screen of the prior arc — child does not initiate the download. Cache lives in documentDirectory (NOT cacheDirectory — iOS may silently purge the latter per Apple dev forum 107071). LRU eviction when cache approaches 3 GB ceiling. Current arc is pinned and never evicts. Per-module SHA-256 content_hash verify on cache read catches partial-download corruption. Preemptive storage check at session start — if device free space < 500 MB, refuse new-arc download and warn parent. See SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md and APP_ARCHITECTURE_MASTER_v1.md.

--- AMENDMENT 2026-04-20 (V1 Scope Condensation) ---
V1 arc count is 8 (Arc 8 Hopegrove / Benson cut per V1_CREATURE_SET_5_OLIVER_AT_M3). Arc-at-a-time delivery mechanism unchanged — same mechanism applies to 8 arcs instead of 9. Post-launch arcs may re-expand the catalog; V1 ship = 8 arcs.

decision_name: Per-module size budget: 60 MB target, 80 MB ceiling, per-module SHORTCUT exception clause
decision_text: Per-module atomic MP4 (per LD-280 SINGLE_MP4_ATOMIC_V1) TARGET is 60 MB; hard CEILING is 80 MB. Resolves the ambiguity between SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md §4.1 (which proposed 100 MB pre-single-MP4) and APP_ARCHITECTURE_MASTER_v1.md §4 (which proposed 80 MB post-single-MP4). 2+2 debate (4 agents, 2026-04-18) converged on 80 MB ceiling: (a) SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT §4.4 sensitivity table explicitly shows 100 MB -> 5.4 GB catalog -> 2.2 GB must evict under LD-282's 3 GB cache ceiling, labeled 'user re-downloads often'; (b) the 100 MB case rested on double-counted Phase B math — Phase B is audio over near-static image, the video track encodes tiny with `-tune stillimage`, contribution dominated by 7 MB audio not 12+ MB full-motion video; (c) M1 measured footprint ~22 MB with 3.6x headroom at 80 MB ceiling; (d) Rule 19 requires specific justification, not speculative future-proofing. EXCEPTION CLAUSE: if any specific late-arc climactic module (Arc 6-9) genuinely requires >80 MB after production optimization, register `SHORTCUT_MODULE_{module_id}_CEILING_V1` in prod_locked_decisions with per-module justification, estimated savings_MB, and closure plan. Do NOT silently exceed ceiling — the exception is the paper trail. Production pipeline ffmpeg default should target 1.5 Mbps H.264 720p for motion / 1.0 Mbps for static content / 128 kbps MP3 mono Phase B audio / WebP q80 ≤1280px for still images — unchanged from SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT §5. Module duration MUST NOT exceed 7 minutes (added 2026-04-28) to mathematically guarantee the 80 MB ceiling at 1.5 Mbps motion bitrate (1.5 Mbps x 7 min x 60s = 78.75 MB inside ceiling). SHORTCUT exception clause for late-arc climactic modules (per-module LD with Kim approval, must include both size override AND duration override).
notes: | 2026-04-28: 7-min duration cap added per v6 §4 (last_modified_date=2026-04-28)

decision_name: Normalization before concat (single-MP4 assembly)
decision_text:
NORMALIZATION_BEFORE_CONCAT_V1 — Each beat's final selected clip MUST be re-encoded to a standardized codec spec before it is eligible for concat into a module MP4. Produced file: `beat_NN_normalized.mp4` sibling to the selected source clip.

WHY. Per LD-280 (RENDERING_ARCHITECTURE_SINGLE_MP4_ATOMIC_V1), every module ships as one atomic MP4 built via ffmpeg concat demuxer. Concat demuxer requires identical codec params across inputs or it silently re-encodes (fidelity drift) or fails. Today per-beat outputs come from heterogeneous pipelines: ByteDance LipSync outputs (one set of params), raw Kling outputs (different params), hand-looped Option A re-encodes (yet another set). Without a normalization step, concat is non-deterministic.

TARGET CODEC SPEC (canonical — this is the SIZE_BUDGET v-spec aligned target).
- Video: H.264 High profile, pixel format `yuv420p`, resolution 1280x720 (720p), constant frame rate 24 fps, CRF 20 (or target bitrate 1.5 Mbps via `-b:v 1.5M -maxrate 1.8M -bufsize 3M` when rate-locked delivery is needed), GOP 48, `-preset slow`.
- Audio: AAC, 128 kbps, mono, 44.1 kHz sample rate.
- Container: MP4 with `-movflags +faststart`, `-pix_fmt yuv420p`, explicit `-r 24`, explicit `-ar 44100 -ac 1`.
- SAR/DAR: force `setsar=1:1`; pad to 1280x720 via `scale=1280:720:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1280:720:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=black`.

CANONICAL FFMPEG COMMAND (single source of truth).
```
ffmpeg -y -i INPUT.mp4   -vf "scale=1280:720:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=1280:720:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=black,setsar=1:1,fps=24"   -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p -preset slow -crf 20 -g 48   -c:a aac -b:a 128k -ar 44100 -ac 1   -movflags +faststart   beat_NN_normalized.mp4
```
Any deviation from this command (different resolution, different codec, different audio params) MUST be registered as a separate LD keyed `NORMALIZATION_EXCEPTION_*` referencing this LD — no silent per-beat tuning.

WHERE IN PIPELINE (option D — hybrid cached + invalidated on source change).
- Trigger 1 (automatic): immediately after a successful lipsync output is produced for a beat (post-lipsync-commit event in production_state). Consumes the lipsync output as source.
- Trigger 2 (automatic): when `selected_option` for a beat changes in `production_state.json`. The new selection's source file drives a re-normalization.
- Trigger 3 (manual fallback): a `/api/beat/normalize` endpoint + storyboard-overlay "Normalize Beat" / "Normalize All" button to force a re-run when cache is suspect (debug/recovery only).
- Blocking: `/api/scene/assemble` (LD-139 STITCH_ARCHITECTURE_MULTI_STAGE) MUST refuse to run until every beat in the event has a valid `beat_NN_normalized.mp4` matching the current `selected_option`. The concat step reads ONLY normalized outputs, never raw lipsync/Kling outputs.

CACHE + INVALIDATION.
- Cache sidecar: `beat_NN_normalized.meta.json` next to the normalized MP4. Contents: `{source_path, source_mtime, source_sha256_first_1mb, selected_option, codec_spec_hash, created_at, normalizer_version}`.
- Cache HIT conditions (all must match): source file path, mtime, SHA-256 of first 1 MB of source, selected_option, codec_spec_hash. Any mismatch → re-normalize.
- Invalidation triggers: source mtime change, selected_option change, codec_spec_hash change (when this LD's spec is versioned up).
- Idempotency: ffmpeg re-encode is not byte-deterministic, but resulting codec params are byte-deterministic under our command. Concat correctness — not encoder bit-exactness — is what matters. Running normalization twice on the same input produces two MP4s with the SAME codec header, which is sufficient.

ERROR HANDLING.
- If ffmpeg fails: write `beat_NN_normalized.error.json` with stderr excerpt + exit code. Do NOT write a partial MP4. Stitch step blocks with a clear human-readable error naming the beat + the error file.
- If source file is missing: log error, block stitch, prompt operator.
- Partial-write protection: normalize to `beat_NN_normalized.mp4.tmp`, then `os.replace()` to final filename. Matches LD-134 `ATOMIC_DOWNLOAD_TMP_RENAME` pattern.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING LDS.
- Extends LD-139 `STITCH_ARCHITECTURE_MULTI_STAGE`: `/api/beat/finalize` applies trim + audio_delay + selected_lipsync; normalization is the STEP AFTER finalize (and after lipsync-commit), STEP BEFORE `/api/scene/assemble`. The LD-139 flow becomes: finalize → [normalize] → concat.
- Serves LD-280 `RENDERING_ARCHITECTURE_SINGLE_MP4_ATOMIC_V1`: the atomic MP4 delivered to the app is the product of normalized beats being concatenated — LD-280 is the "why," this LD is the "how the concat inputs actually match."
- Does NOT touch LD-162 lipsync-source rules (§8.2), LD-172/177/180 start-end pipeline (§8.3), or LD-196 Phase B audio stitch recipe. Normalization runs AFTER those produce their outputs, as a common re-encode tail.
- Compatible with LD-134 (atomic tmp-rename download pattern) and LD-138 (image override durability) — reuses the fcntl+atomic-write contract.

WHAT THIS FORBIDS.
- Concat demuxer inputs that are NOT `beat_NN_normalized.mp4` files. Any path in `/api/scene/assemble` that reads raw lipsync/Kling/hand-looped clips directly is a shortcut per Rule 19 and rejected.
- Per-beat "skip normalization because this one beat's codec already matches." Normalization is uniform — no heuristic opt-out. The cache makes same-spec re-runs cheap, so the short-circuit isn't needed.
- Normalizing as a side-effect inside `/api/scene/assemble`. Normalization is an explicit step with its own cache + error file; assemble only consumes already-normalized inputs.

IMPLEMENTATION OWNER.
- Server-side normalization implementation is a SEPARATE task (not this cascade). This LD specifies the contract; a future session wires `_handle_normalize_beat` in `production_server.py` and adds the blocking check to `_handle_scene_assemble`.

CLOSURE / VALIDATION.
- Closure test: concat 11 normalized beats from Event_1 → resulting MP4 opens in QuickTime with no codec warnings, has continuous audio, passes `ffprobe` identical-codec-param check across all streams, and size is within SIZE_BUDGET_VIDEO_V1 target (≤ 1.5 Mbps average).
- Non-closure: if the resulting MP4 shows any of (audio desync, glitch frames at beat boundaries, audio dropouts, varying resolution between beats, varying frame rate), that is a normalization failure — not a concat failure — and the normalization step is the fix location.

decision_name: Session state persistence + child-authored graceful resume
decision_text:
App MUST persist session state to Firestore every 5s during Phase B: {module_id, phase, timestamp_ms, audio_position_ms, child_id}. On app relaunch, if session_state.active == true AND age < 30min, show Chipper prompt offering child the choice: pick up where we were, or start fresh. Child-authored choice is load-bearing — ages 7-11 with trauma/anxiety backgrounds need autonomy for regulation, not forced resume. AsyncStorage fallback for offline crash. Mandatory before any real-user launch (not nice-to-have). Rationale from 4+4 viral-scale debate (preflight 87): mid-Phase-B crash was the only CATASTROPHIC safety finding the counter-agents didn't strip — a trauma kid who settled then got dumped to a blank screen destroys the app's nervous-system safety. No shortcut acceptable per Rule 19.

AMENDMENT 2026-04-19 (restated, not superseded): Layer 1 default is RESUME_MODE='silent-resume' per preflight 111 and MODULE_EXIT_AND_PROGRESSION_V1. Scope: RESUME_MODE governs automatic resume after app crash, force-quit, or OS-kill at re-launch only — consulted by findInProgressSession() at app startup. It does NOT govern explicit child-authored buttons. The "Start Magic Spell Again" button (always visible during Phase B range, seeks to phase_b.start_ms) and the Exit button (pauses + returns to map) are unconditional child actions independent of RESUME_MODE. Infrastructure unchanged from v1; only default UX flipped from modal-prompt to silent-resume, since the forthcoming menu UI will provide the resume-or-fresh choice at the correct user-visible surface.

decision_name: iPad 9th gen memory benchmark gate before any user ship
decision_text:
Empirical OOM benchmark on physical iPad 9th gen (A13 Bionic, 3 GB RAM) MUST pass before first user ship. Test protocol: run Module 1 + Module 2 back-to-back on an iPad 9 with 2 GB free RAM (simulating parent device with other apps resident). Profile peak memory via Xcode Instruments during: (a) M1 cold launch, (b) M1 Phase B playback, (c) M1→M2 transition, (d) M2 Phase B. Pass criteria: no OOM kill; peak RSS < 500 MB for Phase B playback; peak < 600 MB for story scene. Fail → halt ship, investigate (codec/bitrate/decoder buffer) before retry. Rationale from 4+4 viral-scale debate (preflight 87): this was the ONE unquantified scale risk that 4 advocate lenses missed and Counter 2 surfaced. APP_ARCHITECTURE_MASTER §10 already flagged iPad 9 memory as residual + unbenchmarked. No structural mitigation exists post-ship if OOM appears in the wild.

decision_name: Async queue between parent signup + KWS verification + therapist-visible status
decision_text: KWS COPPA consent verification MUST run through a Cloud Tasks async queue, NOT synchronous inline with parent signup. Pattern: parent submits consent → Firestore consent_queue doc → CF processes with exponential backoff + DLQ → parent sees 'Your consent is pending, you'll get email within X minutes. You can close the app.' (NEVER 'try again later'). Therapist dashboard shows each family's onboarding status live so therapist can triage in-clinic. Prevents: (a) in-clinic humiliation if KWS lags during a scheduled setup session, (b) support flood — 80% of support tickets in a surge window are 'is my consent through yet?' Rationale from 4+4 viral-scale debate (preflight 87): genuine structural decision — 3 advocates + 2 counters converged that this is not a tuning knob, it's an architectural pattern (queue + dashboard visibility). Rule 19 applies: synchronous KWS = error path open at scale.

decision_name: MindfulNest lifetime size/performance budget (v1, 2026-04-18)
decision_text: Lifetime size/performance budget governing what ships to users. Initial App Store download ≤150 MB target / 200 MB hard ceiling (iOS cellular install cap). Per-module streamed payload ≤60 MB target / 80 MB ceiling (per LD-283 SIZE_BUDGET_PER_MODULE_V1; supersedes SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md §4.1's preliminary 100 MB ceiling, which was pre-single-MP4 and double-counted Phase B math). On-device cache ceiling 3 GB (LRU eviction; pinned: active module + active arc shared assets). 54-module total catalog ≤6 GB. Lowest-supported device iPad 9th gen (A13 Bionic, 2021, 64 GB base, 3 GB RAM). Video: H.264 High 720p @ 1.5 Mbps motion / 1.0 Mbps static, 2.0 Mbps hard ceiling — see SIZE_BUDGET_VIDEO_V1. Audio: Phase B mix MP3 128 kbps mono 44.1 kHz; voice stems 192 kbps intermediate only; ambient beds OGG 96 kbps — see SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIO_V1. Images: masters 2048×2048 PNG live in /masters/ and NEVER ship; delivery variants WebP q80 long-edge ≤1280 px — see SIZE_BUDGET_IMAGE_V1. CI bundle gate: see BUNDLE_SIZE_CI_ENFORCEMENT_V1. Source: SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md §2/§4/§5. Parent decision; child siblings = SIZE_BUDGET_VIDEO_V1, SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIO_V1, SIZE_BUDGET_IMAGE_V1, BUNDLE_SIZE_CI_ENFORCEMENT_V1. Per-module ceiling overrides require SHORTCUT_MODULE_{id}_CEILING_V1 paper trail per LD-283.

decision_name: Video codec + bitrate target (H.264 High 720p, 1.5 Mbps motion / 1.0 Mbps static / 2.0 Mbps hard ceiling)
decision_text: All shipped video assets (atomic per-module MP4 per LD-280, normalized per-beat clips per LD-284): H.264 High profile, yuv420p, +faststart (moov at head). Resolution: 1280×720 (default) or 1080×810 (Phase A 4:3 framing). Bitrate targets: full-motion story scene 1.5 Mbps; static / slow pan / Phase A establishing 1.0 Mbps; HARD CEILING 2.0 Mbps — anything above MUST be re-encoded or justified via SHORTCUT_VIDEO_BITRATE_OVERRIDE_{asset_id} in prod_locked_decisions. ffmpeg reference command (single source of truth): `ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -c:v libx264 -preset slow -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p -b:v 1500k -maxrate 1800k -bufsize 3000k -movflags +faststart -c:a aac -b:a 96k -ac 2 -ar 44100 out.mp4`. Post-encode VERIFICATION: ffprobe stream bit_rate MUST be ≤1,900,000 bps (5% guard band below 2.0 Mbps ceiling, accounts for VBR drift); HARD FAIL otherwise. No HEVC for MVP (defer post-MVP — H.264 is iOS-native, hardware-decoded on A13). No 4K. Source: SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md §5.1. Child of SIZE_BUDGET_V1.

decision_name: Audio bitrate target (Phase B mix 128 kbps mono MP3; voice stems 192 kbps intermediate; ambient beds 96 kbps OGG/AAC)
decision_text: All shipped audio assets: Phase B final mix MP3 128 kbps mono 44.1 kHz (saves ~33% vs 192 kbps with no perceptible difference on iPad speakers; HARD CEILING 160 kbps for any module-final mix). Voice stems (intermediate, NOT shipped) keep 192 kbps mono — ElevenLabs default. Ambient beds / SFX in shared library: OGG Vorbis 96 kbps (better quality per bit for looping beds; AAC-LC 96 kbps acceptable alternative; HARD CEILING 128 kbps). Stereo only if ambient bed clearly benefits — most don't on iPad speakers; default mono. Silence compression per CLAUDE.md §8.4 (silence >1.0s → 0.8s, -32 dB / 150 ms threshold) saves additional 3–5% per Phase B mix; keep enabled. Note: AAC 128 kbps mono is the canonical post-normalization audio per LD-284 (concat demuxer requires AAC); MP3 is the pre-normalization mix format. Source: SIZE_BUDGET_AUDIT_20260418.md §5.2. decision_name: Image masters/delivery split (2048 PNG masters never ship; WebP q80 ≤1280px ships)
decision_text: Image asset two-tier model. MASTER tier: 2048×2048 PNG (alpha where needed). Lives in /masters/ subdirectory of Production/Event_N/ or Production/Character_Assets/. NEVER ships to app. Required for cropping quality floor and FLUX Kontext consistency. DELIVERY tier: WebP q80, long-edge ≤1280 px (hero stills) or q75 (background tiles). decision_name: Stripe idempotency: dual-path (outbound API + inbound webhook) keyed to prevent $499 double-charge
decision_text:
All Stripe integration code MUST implement idempotency on BOTH paths to prevent the $499 one-time double-charge product-specific load-bearing failure mode. Single-clause idempotency-by-event.id covers ONLY webhook redelivery and leaves three other double-charge paths open: (a) client-side double-submit producing two distinct legitimate event.ids, (b) Checkout Session re-creation after network blip producing a second legitimate Session that completes, (c) refund-then-recharge race where webhook ordering creates ledger inconsistency. Therefore TWO clauses are mandatory and inseparable:

CLAUSE 1 (outbound) — every Stripe API call that creates a financial event (PaymentIntent.create, Checkout.Session.create, Subscription.create, Charge.create, Refund.create) MUST set the Stripe-Idempotency-Key header to a deterministic key of form `{childId}:{sku}:{attemptSeq}` where attemptSeq is incremented ONLY after a definitive failure (4xx, 5xx, or timeout-with-retry-budget-exhausted). This blocks client double-submit and Session re-creation paths. Stripe holds idempotency results 24h.

CLAUSE 2 (inbound) — every webhook handler MUST treat event.id as the dedup key. On receipt: SELECT FROM stripe_events WHERE event_id = ?. If row exists, return 200 OK no-op. If not, INSERT row in same transaction as the business-logic write (Firestore tx OR Cloud Functions transaction). This blocks redelivery and out-of-order race paths.

Both clauses required — neither alone is sufficient. Severity HIGH because financial-harm to a parent who paid $499 is reputation-ending for a B2C-via-therapist trust model. Source: Phase 0 4+4 review preflight id=100, session decision id=35. Enforcement: Stripe webhook handler implementation; Cloud Function deploy-time grep-check for both Stripe-Idempotency-Key header presence (CLAUSE 1) and event.id dedup table read (CLAUSE 2). Refunds rationale: refund-then-recharge race is also closed because both the refund and the recharge are outbound calls subject to CLAUSE 1's deterministic key, so a second legit recharge requires a deliberate attemptSeq bump rather than a silent retry.

decision_name: Real-ffmpeg integration tests required for any ffmpeg orchestration module
decision_text: Any production module that constructs ffmpeg/ffprobe argv lists and shells out MUST ship a companion real-ffmpeg integration test file that invokes the actual binaries against synthetic lavfi fixtures. Mocked subprocess.run tests validate argv construction and state machines; they CANNOT catch filtergraph collisions, invalid flag combinations, codec/format mismatches, stream-specifier errors, or concat demuxer failures. Bug 3 (-vf + -filter_complex collision, rc=234) shipped under LD 294 with 16 green mocked tests because real ffmpeg was never invoked in CI. decision_name: Non-motion-locking tail for lipsync-targeted beats
decision_text: Lipsync-targeted beats (beat.lipsync_targeted=True, default for Event_1 per LD-180) now use 'no dialogue in video' as the Rule 8.1-required tail. Sprite-pipeline beats (lipsync_targeted=False) retain the motion-locking 'Silent subtle idle movement only' tail. Both are Rule 8.1-allowed alternatives. The switch removes the 'only' motion-lock for narrative content while preserving idle-loop stability for sprites. decision_name: Artificial (local) timeouts never mark tasks failed. Vendor verdict only. Orphan submissions auto-recover.
decision_text: Kim directive 2026-04-19 17:48 UTC: 'dont let our artificial timeouts create blocks.' The old behavior marked a WaveSpeed animation option FAILED after 4 transport-class timeouts (urlopen timed out, connection reset, SSL hiccups). That made Kim's local HTTP timeout the authoritative failure verdict, which is wrong — the vendor may still be processing. NEW BEHAVIOR (production_server.py `_handle_transient_failure`): (1) Transport errors (timeouts, URLError, OSError, SSL issues) NEVER mark status=failed. They just set next_attempt_at_epoch and keep polling indefinitely with capped 60s backoff. (2) Only err.startswith('wavespeed reported failure') is authoritative — that's the vendor saying the job itself failed, which DOES transition status=failed. (3) MAX_RETRIES no longer caps transport retries (still caps the logic branch for the pre-fail CDN probe schedule, which remains useful as an early rescue). COMPLEMENTARY: new OrphanSweepThread (production_server.py) runs every 60s and scans state for mid-submission crashes — entries with status='submitting' AND task_id=None AND submitted_at_epoch older than ORPHAN_SUBMIT_THRESHOLD_SEC (5 min). Recovers both animation options and lipsync (preserving last-known-good file reference on lipsync) so UI Send for Lipsync button is clickable again without manual state surgery. Every recovery logged to stdout. SHIPPED ALONGSIDE: (a) WaveSpeed poll timeout 30->90s; (b) Pre-fail CDN probe timeout 10->60s; (c) Pre-fail CDN probe now fires on FIRST poll failure ({2,4} -> {1,2,4}); (d) ByteDance LipSync poll timeout 15->60s (lipsync_sender.py:394). VERIFICATION: 24 preview_stitched tests + existing Tier 1B tests green. Server restart clean. Backups: production_server.py.bak_poll_timeout_20260419T174002Z + lipsync_sender unchanged-backup available. Parent: preflight 107. Complements LD 311 (WAVESPEED_POLL_TIMEOUT_RAISE_20260419).

decision_name: Lipsync polling survives server restarts (LipsyncPollingThread daemon)
decision_text: Kim session 2026-04-19 17:15 UTC: submitted beat_03 lipsync, then a server restart (for Move-to-A UI fix) killed the in-flight HTTP handler's poll_until_done loop. ByteDance completed the task ~98s after submit but our state stayed 'polling' for 2.5+ hours. Manual rescue: queried WaveSpeed directly, downloaded CDN output, updated state. ROOT CAUSE: lipsync polling ran inline in the /api/lipsync HTTP handler's thread. Animation polling uses PollingThread (persistent daemon, restarts independently at server startup). Lipsync had no equivalent. FIX: new LipsyncPollingThread daemon started at server startup alongside PollingThread + OrphanSweepThread. Sweeps every LIPSYNC_POLL_INTERVAL_SEC=30s for all beats with lipsync.status=='polling' AND task_id set. For each, queries WaveSpeed (ByteDance LipSync uses the shared /v3/predictions endpoint). On 'completed' downloads output URL to beat.lipsync.file path and writes state via state.mutate_state. On 'failed' marks lipsync.status='failed'. Transport errors are no-op and retry next cycle (Preflight 107 principle: artificial timeouts never block). Stamps 'recovered_by=lipsync_poller_persistent' + 'recovered_at' for auditability. FILES: Production/tools/production_server.py (LipsyncPollingThread class ~+100 LOC; startup wiring next to OrphanSweepThread). No tests added this cycle — covered structurally by the existing OrphanSweepThread unit tests pattern; integration-tested live today by rescue of beat_03 lipsync. Backups: production_server.py.bak_swap_to_a_20260419T182446Z; beat_03_lipsync.mp4.bak_before_rescue_20260419T211810Z. Parent preflight 109. Complements LD 312 (NO_ARTIFICIAL_TIMEOUT_BLOCKS) — same principle applied to lipsync.

decision_name: Preview normalize cache now mtime-aware; lipsync poller uses flush=True + unbuffered stdout
decision_text: TWO RELATED FIXES. (1) Preview stitched cache staleness — Kim hit 'Preview All Stitched shows old video after lipsync rescue'. Root cause: _handle_preview_stitched only checked `if not norm.is_file()` before rebuilding per-beat normalized clips. When a lipsync rescue updated animation_clips/*.mp4 mid-session, the normalized intermediate still existed from hours earlier so the pipeline reused it and baked the OLD content into the preview. Fix: also rebuild when src.stat().st_mtime > dst.stat().st_mtime. (2) LipsyncPollingThread silent failures — after shipping the daemon (LD 314), kim saw zero log output even though beat_02 lipsync completed on ByteDance and the daemon should have caught it. Root causes: (a) print() calls in daemon threads inherit stdout buffering; with nohup redirecting to a file, lines never flushed until process exit; (b) the 'still processing' branch was silent so there was no way to distinguish 'no candidates' from 'stuck'. Fix: added flush=True to all [lipsync-poller] prints; added per-cycle heartbeat line that lists candidates; added status log on every poll result; relaunched server with `python3 -u` to force unbuffered mode as a belt-and-suspenders guard. decision_name: Module exit, progression gate, Start Magic Spell Again button, Reward section
decision_text:
Governing behavior for module playback exit, progression-to-next-stage gating, Phase B restart, Win video, Reward section, and backpack item reveal. Parent architectural LDs: LD-280 (single-MP4 atomic), LD-281 (no runtime TTS), LD-282 (arc-at-a-time delivery), LD-286 (session state persistence), LD-164 (awardCoinsOnSession), LD-100 (ownedItems placement), LD-102 (decorationReward always earned).

SEVEN LOCKED RULES:

1. EXIT BUTTON: available on all playing video sections (Intro, Phase A, Phase B, Win video). Press = pause expo-video player, save current position to AsyncStorage session_state_v1:<moduleId>, return child to map screen. Stage remains LOCKED (next stage not unlocked) until MP4 plays to onEnd.

2. PROGRESSION GATE: the module's next stage unlocks ONLY when expo-video fires onEnd on the module MP4. X-out mid-play leaves the stage locked; child can re-enter and resume until they play through to onEnd.

3. RESUME: on app crash, force-quit, or OS-kill re-launch, findInProgressSession seeks to saved position regardless of phase. RESUME_MODE default is 'silent-resume' per LD-286 amendment 2026-04-19. On explicit re-entry from menu/map: same seek-to-saved-position behavior. Phase-agnostic — no auto-restart of Phase B on resume.

4. PHASE B RESTART BUTTON (child-facing label: "Start Magic Spell Again" — Everdale narrative framing, techniques are magic spells): always visible at top of screen during phase_b range (per manifest.phase_boundaries entry where name === 'phase_b'). Pressing seeks to phase_b.start_ms. Unconditional child action — ignores RESUME_MODE. Operates during live Phase B playback AND after resume from saved position. The child-facing label "Start Magic Spell Again" is the ONLY acceptable UI string for this button; do NOT use "Restart Phase B" or any debugging/internal term in any child-facing surface.

5. WIN VIDEO: plays as the final section of the module MP4 (baked per LD-280). No special client behavior vs other video phases. onEnd firing here triggers the app to write /sessions/{sessionId} with completionStatus='completed', which fires awardCoinsOnSession Cloud Function (LD-164) to persist coins + decoration + special items.

6. REWARD SECTION: stock React Native screen (NOT video) rendered after module MP4 onEnd. Animates coin counter + item drop into backpack. Rewards are already persisted by awardCoinsOnSession CF before or as animation plays — rewards are GUARANTEED. X-out during reward section = return to map, items already in backpack. The reward-section celebration animation itself is one-time and not replayable. HOWEVER: when a new item first appears in the backpack UI (whether the child viewed the reward section or X'd out of it), the backpack renders a small reveal animation (swell / glow / pop-in) as the new-item acknowledgement. This ensures the child always sees a moment of recognition for newly-earned items, even if they skipped the reward section. This backpack-level reveal is orthogonal to the module-playback system — it bridges the reward-acquisition event with the decorative-space/backpack UI.

7. DECORATIVE SPACE: orthogonal to module playback. Placement state governed by LD-100 (unified ownedItems[].placedIn) and LD-102 (decorationReward always earned). Not affected by module exit behavior.

Upstream dependency: Track B (single-MP4 assembly) manifest format must carry phase_boundaries: [{name, start_ms, end_ms}] per phase — names intro / phase_a / phase_b / win_video. New requirement on ffmpeg assembly step.

Implementation status: forward-spec. PR #16 ships base infrastructure (useModulePlayback + sessionState + cacheIndex). Exit button, "Start Magic Spell Again" button, progression-gate logic, Reward section UI, backpack reveal animation — all follow-up work tracked as prod_blockers per Task 7 of preflight 111.

Implementation tracked by prod_blockers id=10. Unblocks on satisfying all 6 closure criteria.

--- AMENDMENT 2026-04-20 (V1 Scope Condensation) ---
Exit/progression mechanism unchanged. Reward section routes to backpack per BACKPACK_IS_COLLECTION_GALLERY_V1 (no separate creatures-met UI). Backpack reveal animation remains open blocker (pre-existing LD-316 Layer 1 open items + new V1 blockers).

decision_name: Auto pre-roll padding in silcomp pipeline (AUTO_PREROLL_V1)
decision_text: Problem: ElevenLabs TTS regen typically produces audio that starts speaking within ~125ms of t=0. ByteDance LatentSync needs ~300-400ms of leading silence to lock onto mouth landmarks before the first phoneme, otherwise the first sentence appears with no mouth movement in the lipsync output. Kim repeatedly hit this all day; manual padding was ephemeral because Regen Audio overwrote the padded file. Solution (Preflight 110, 1+1 agent debate): fold auto pre-roll detection + padding into _silcomp_audio. New constants: _AUTO_PREROLL_MIN_S=0.300, _AUTO_PREROLL_TARGET_S=0.400, _AUTO_PREROLL_PROBE_WINDOW_S=0.500, _AUTO_PREROLL_RMS_THRESHOLD_DB=-32.0. Detection: new _detect_head_silence_s() uses ffmpeg astats (per Counter Finding 1 — silencedetect is head-blind when audio starts above threshold). Falls back to silencedetect within the 500ms probe window to pin the exact silence end. Padding: if head silence < 300ms, prepend anullsrc segment to bring total leading silence to 400ms. Implementation folded into silcomp's existing concat-demuxer machinery (Counter recommendation: one ffmpeg cycle, not two). Returns preroll_processing metadata dict with applied/reason/preroll_added_s fields. Gating (Counter Findings 3+4): auto_preroll only fires when caller passes auto_preroll=True. _handle_lipsync_submit sets it to True ONLY when phase_1.trim_start == 0 (trim_start>0 means Kim intentionally skipped settling frames; preroll would undo that). Also passes max_audio_s to clamp the preroll if it would push padded audio past the video window ceiling. skip_auto_preroll body flag allows explicit opt-out. Verification: smoke-tested both paths (no-preroll audio gets 400ms pad applied; 2s-healthy audio correctly no-ops). Server restarted PID visible in log. Parent preflight 110. Complements LD 311/312/314/315 (the lipsync reliability chain).

decision_name: Dynamic range compression + EBU R128 loudness normalization added to silcomp pipeline
decision_text: Kim session 2026-04-19 22:45 UTC: after AUTO_PREROLL_V1 shipped, beat_05 lipsync STILL had no mouth movement on 'Oh it's silly'. Root cause isolated via astats RMS probe: ElevenLabs renders quiet phrases (hesitations) at -30 dB while rest of dialogue is at -18 to -22 dB. ByteDance LatentSync's internal audio gate treats sub-30 dB as silence → zero mouth animation. Pre-roll helped marginally but didn't solve the underlying audio-level issue. FIX: two-stage filter chain applied in _silcomp_audio output: (1) dynaudnorm=f=200:g=5:p=0.95:m=15 — dynamic range compression, boosts quiet phrases up to 15x (empirically tuned on Kim's real audio; lifted -30 dB quiet part to -15 dB); (2) loudnorm=I=-16:TP=-1.5:LRA=8 — EBU R128 loudness normalization, locks output to -16 LUFS for consistent perceived loudness across modules. Both paths covered: passthrough (no silences) applies loudnorm via a single -af pass; concat path (silences compressed OR preroll added) applies loudnorm to the final concat output. Gated on loudnorm=True param passed by _handle_lipsync_submit; opt-out via body.skip_loudnorm. Metadata surfaced in state.lipsync.audio_processing: loudnorm_applied bool + target params. VERIFICATION: real-ffmpeg empirical test on Kim's line_05_tessa.mp3 showed quiet phrase boost from -24 dB to -15 dB (well above LatentSync's -30 dB gate). 24/24 preview_stitched tests + 11/11 swap tests all green. Single-pass design (no measurement pass); adds ~100-200ms overhead per submission. Parent preflight 113. Chains with LDs 311/312/314/315/317 for full lipsync reliability.

decision_name: Bug fix: mixed-path preview stitcher now head-trims incoming beat by previous pair's fade (duplicate-frame class)
decision_text: Kim symptom 2026-04-19: with per-beat fade override (LD 320 / preflight 117) set so beat_10.fade_after_ms=500, the resulting beat_11 playback started with 'OK' (from the xfade_pair crossfade) then REPEATED 'OK kiddo...' (the first 500ms of beat_11 body playing again). Classic duplicate-frame-at-concat-boundary bug. Root cause: the subagent-shipped mixed-path loop at production_server.py:7149+ only applied trim_tail to the OUTGOING side of each xfade pair; the INCOMING beat's head was never trimmed. With per-beat fades this was a real bug. (It didn't manifest with all-equal-global fades because the old code path had different shape.) Fix: new helper `trim_body(src, dst, head_remove_s, tail_remove_s)` in lib/ffmpeg_stitch.py that does both trims in one ffmpeg pass. Mixed-path loop refactored so each beat N sets:   head_remove_s = clamped_pair_fades[N-1]/1000 if N>0 and prev pair had fade>0, else 0   tail_remove_s = clamped_pair_fades[N]/1000 if N<last and next pair has fade>0, else 0 Invariants preserved: first beat never head-trimmed (nothing fades in), last beat never tail-trimmed (Counter (f) CRITICAL — preview ends on actual final frame). Verification: 180/180 tests green (zero regressions). trim_body real-ffmpeg smoke test confirmed head+tail atomic trim produces correct duration (2.2s from 3s src with 0.5s head + 0.3s tail). Empty-trim case raises ValueError as designed. Server restarted. Stale body/xfade/preview_stitched caches purged so next preview rebuilds with corrected logic. Backups: production_server.py.bak_headtrim_20260420T013512Z + ffmpeg_stitch.py.bak_headtrim_20260420T013512Z. trim_body naming stays ITEM-AGNOSTIC — V4 7-segment assembly (LD-280) will use the same helper unchanged. Parent preflight 118. Complements LD 320 (per-beat fade override).

decision_name: Firebase functions:secrets:set requires manual CI SA IAM binding
decision_text:
After every `firebase functions:secrets:set <SECRET_NAME>`, the CI/deploy service account must be manually granted `secretmanager` permissions or `firebase deploy --only functions --dry-run` CI checks will fail with HTTP 403 "Permission 'secretmanager.secrets.get' denied." Firebase's command only grants `secretmanager.secretAccessor` to the Cloud Functions RUNTIME service account, not to the CI/deploy SA.

REQUIRED RUNBOOK (two grants, both required):

1. Per-secret VALUE access:
   gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding <SECRET_NAME>      --member="serviceAccount:github-actions-deployer@mindfulnestkids.iam.gserviceaccount.com"      --role="roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"      --project=mindfulnestkids

2. Project-level METADATA access (one-time, covers all future secrets):
   gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding mindfulnestkids      --member="serviceAccount:github-actions-deployer@mindfulnestkids.iam.gserviceaccount.com"      --role="roles/secretmanager.viewer"      --condition=None

WHY TWO ROLES: `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` grants `secretmanager.versions.access` (read value) but NOT `secretmanager.secrets.get` (read metadata). `firebase deploy --dry-run` needs BOTH because it checks secret existence first. The `viewer` role provides the missing `secrets.get`.

IAM propagation takes ~60s after the gcloud commands complete. First CI re-run may still 403; wait one minute and retry.

Discovered 2026-04-19 during PR #21 (Stripe) CI unblock. Three successive `firebase deploy --dry-run` failures until both roles were granted. Evidence: activity logs 1035 (initial failure), 1042 (IAM grant), 1044 (PR #21 merged after fix propagated).

APPLIES TO: mindfulnestkids project, github-actions-deployer SA, any future secret provisioned via `firebase functions:secrets:set` that is consumed by Cloud Functions during deploy (currently: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET). ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (now-dead per LD-281) would have needed this too.

CROSS-REFERENCES: LD-208 RENT_DOPPLER_SECRETS (primary secret store); LD-300 STRIPE_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_V1 (first consumer that surfaced the issue); LD-291 PARENT_COACH_MIN_INSTANCES_V1 (another future consumer); LD-126 HARDENED_SESSION_PROTOCOL_TERMINAL_CLI (secret provisioning requires terminal CLI anyway).

Complements: LD-208 (Doppler) + LD-300/301 (Stripe + parent_coach CF secrets).
Supersedes: none.

decision_name: Handoff §A pre-auths do NOT satisfy runtime classifier for production deploys
decision_text: The problem: handoff §A "pre-granted by Kim" enumeration is a HINT to the subagent session but does NOT override the runtime auto-mode classifier. On 2026-04-20, Stream D's `firebase deploy --only functions:stripeWebhook --project mindfulnestkids` was correctly denied by the classifier with "user's message authorized reading a handoff doc and proceeding generally, not specifically this production deployment" — even though handoff §A had an explicit checkbox for it. The fix: handoffs that authorize production deploys MUST do ONE of: (a) the operator names the specific deploy command in the in-session deployment message at the moment of need (e.g., "proceed, and specifically run `firebase deploy --only functions:X --project Y`"), OR (b) the operator pre-registers a permission rule in `~/.claude/settings.json` matching the exact deploy command shape before firing the handoff. Blanket "all permissions granted" language does NOT work. Rationale: auto-mode classifier is a runtime safety layer ABOVE prompt-level grants (LESSONS_LEARNED §1.4); this is correct behavior. Related: LD-126 HARDENED_SESSION_PROTOCOL, Rule 19 no-shortcuts. Complements: LESSONS_LEARNED §1.4, §2.5 (IAM binding). Kim manually added the settings.json rule for `firebase deploy --only functions:* --project mindfulnestkids:*` on 2026-04-20 to close this specific case. Future handoffs authorizing NEW production-deploy command shapes must repeat either (a) or (b).

decision_name: Therapist module-asset entitlement via bidirectional-invite-linked therapist-child subcollection
decision_text:
Therapist module-asset entitlement MUST be enforced via a bidirectional-invite-linked therapist-child subcollection, NOT via therapist role alone.

RULE SHAPE (Firestore Rules v2 — the implementation session must write exactly this shape into hasArcEntitlementForModule):

function hasArcEntitlementForModule(childId, moduleId) {
  let arc = moduleArcKey(moduleId);
  let parentDoc = get(/databases/$(database)/documents/parents/$(request.auth.uid));
  let isEntitledParent = parentDoc != null && parentDoc.data.entitledArcs.hasAny([arc]);
  let isLinkedTherapist = exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/therapists/$(request.auth.uid)/linkedChildren/$(childId));
  return isEntitledParent || isLinkedTherapist;
}

BIDIRECTIONAL INVITE FLOW (Cloud Function handleInviteAccept — the ONLY writer of /therapists/{tid}/linkedChildren/{cid}):

Flow A (therapist-initiated): therapist creates /invites/{inviteId} with {initiatedBy: therapistId, targetEmail: parentEmail, status: 'pending'}. Parent signs in (existing or new account), system presents invite, parent accepts. CF verifies: (a) invite status='pending', (b) parent auth uid matches an existing or just-created /parents/ doc with email == targetEmail. On success: CF writes /therapists/{therapistId}/linkedChildren/{childId} link doc with provenance metadata + marks invite 'accepted'.

Flow B (parent-initiated): parent creates /invites/{inviteId} with {initiatedBy: parentId, targetEmail: therapistEmail, status: 'pending'}. Therapist signs up (new) or signs in (existing), system presents invite, therapist accepts. CF verifies: (a) invite status='pending', (b) therapist auth uid matches an existing or just-created /therapists/ doc with email == targetEmail. On success: same link doc write as Flow A + invite 'accepted'.

In BOTH flows: link is ONLY created after BOTH parties have acted (send + accept). This is stronger two-sided consent than the original 'parent approves therapist' unilateral model. Neither party can unilaterally create a link.

SECURITY RULES ON /invites/ AND /therapists/{tid}/linkedChildren/{cid}:
- /invites/{inviteId}: CREATE allowed to authenticated users where request.resource.data.initiatedBy == request.auth.uid. UPDATE status='accepted' ONLY by CF (rules deny client writes to status). DELETE by initiator only.
- /therapists/{therapistId}/linkedChildren/{childId}: CREATE + UPDATE + DELETE ALL denied to clients. CF-only writes. READ by linked therapist or linked-child's parent.

V1 ALL-ARCS CLARIFICATION (Kim 2026-04-20): In V1, all paying families receive entitledArcs: ['arc_1'..'arc_9'] populated by the Stripe checkout CF on first payment success. Per-arc gating in hasArcEntitlementForModule is trivially true for any active-program family. The rule shape is forward-looking for V2 (next 10 arcs at separate pricing). Arc-gate semantics come into play in V2.

WHY BIDIRECTIONAL CONSENT IS STRONGER THAN UNILATERAL APPROVAL: Counter-1 (COPPA lens) on 2026-04-20 flagged A1's biggest risk as 'malicious therapist self-links to childIds if link-write pathway isn't parent-consent-gated.' The bidirectional-invite model addresses this structurally: the link write is CF-mediated and requires BOTH initiator and acceptor auth verification. A malicious therapist cannot unilaterally create a link — the CF refuses unless parent has auth'd an acceptance event.

TEST CASES (exact 6 cases the implementation session must add to entitlements.test.js):
1. therapist with /therapists/{uid}/linkedChildren/{cid} reads /modules/{mid}/assets/{aid} where cid has arc entitlement → ALLOW
2. therapist WITHOUT link to cid reads same → DENY
3. parent of cid reads same with entitled arc → ALLOW (regression guard for PR #19 base behavior)
4. parent of cid reads UN-entitled arc → DENY
5. revoked link (doc deleted) — immediate next read → DENY (no staleness window)
6. cross-family leakage: therapist A linked to child B reads child C (unlinked) → DENY

DECISION PROVENANCE: 10-agent convergence 2026-04-20 (5 advocates × 5 approaches: A1 linked-child direct rule, A2 custom claims, A3 mirror collection, A4 defer, A5 shared entitlements doc × 5 counter lenses: COPPA/privilege-escalation, complexity, delivery-risk, testability, reviewer-confidence). 4/5 counters picked A1; C1 (COPPA lens) picked A3 but named A1 as 'acceptable fallback IF link-write pathway is parent-consent-gated' — satisfied by bidirectional-invite CF model. Kim locked 2026-04-20 05:00Z ('Yes go ahead and lock A1 as an LD with an agent and the QA skill').

IMPLEMENTATION HANDLE: prod_blockers #24 (upgraded with this recipe 2026-04-20). Implementation handoff: HANDOFF_A1_THERAPIST_ENTITLEMENT_IMPL_20260420.md (Dropbox project root).

COMPLEMENTS: LD-316 MODULE_EXIT_AND_PROGRESSION_V1 (parent progression LD), LD-325 FOLLOWUP_LD_316_LAYER_2_PROGRESSION_FIRESTORE_MIRROR (Layer 2 companion), LD-326 HANDOFF_AUTH_VS_CLASSIFIER_AUTH_V1 (governance companion), LD-327 APP_REPO_SESSION_DIRECTUS_CRED_LOADING_V1 (governance companion), LD-226 COPPA parent-child nesting, LD-225 data-min allowlists, LD-217 third-party-data gate, LD-171 CF sanitization pattern, LD-89 therapist commissions. SUPERSEDES: none.

ENFORCEMENT TOPOLOGY: This LD alone is NOT sufficient to guarantee correct implementation. Three layers deployed: (L1) this LD + preflight hook auto-surfacing via enforcement_type=governed_file; (L2) prod_blockers #24 description upgraded to inline implementation recipe (rules diff + CF pseudocode + test cases); (L3) pre-written HANDOFF_A1_THERAPIST_ENTITLEMENT_IMPL_20260420.md with CF scaffold scoped. Implementation session needs only to fill in blanks, not design from scratch.

decision_name: V1 retention = backpack + variable reward + map-visit streak + Today card + weekly drops + Parent Weekly Plan
decision_text:
V1 retention has 6 low-coercion mechanisms:
(1) Collection — backpack is THE gallery (see BACKPACK_IS_COLLECTION_GALLERY_V1).
(2) Variable reward — Magic Tap probabilistic drops + fidget-play proportional coins.
(3) Streak — fires on MAP VISIT, not module completion (anti-pattern protection per V1_ANTI_PATTERNS_LOCKED).
(4) Today card — on app open, Chipper surfaces one curated suggestion from content pool.
(5) Weekly content drops post-launch (new items, new dialogue, seasonal elements).
(6) Parent Weekly Plan — 26-week calendar with 2 modules/week target + 5-min daily together-practice.

No push notifications in V1. Retention threads AROUND therapeutic content, never gamifies it. Research backing: Duolingo 3.6x retention from 7-day streak; Neko Atsume variable-reward; Toca Life weekly drops; Mightier collection-layer-over-therapy validated clinically.

decision_name: V1 anti-patterns — no fail states, no module streaks, no pet decay, no aggressive monetization
decision_text:
Locked V1 anti-patterns (require explicit unlock LD to introduce):
(1) No fail states anywhere — fidget zones, modules, Magic Tap all succeed-only.
(2) No tutorials on fidget layer — tap primitives self-evident.
(3) No pet-care decay — creatures do not get sad/hungry/anxious if child doesn't visit.
(4) No points/scores on therapy content — Phase A/B produce no numeric scores, no star ratings, no completion %.
(5) No multi-step fidget mini-games — Path A primitive per PATH_A_TAP_PRIMITIVE_ALL_FIDGETS_V1 is one-step.
(6) No aggressive monetization — no paywalls on therapeutic content, no ads, no limited-time FOMO.
(7) No streak on modules — streak is map-visit-only per RETENTION_LAYER_V1.
(8) No voice substitution — Cedric is Cedric, Chipper is Chipper; runtime TTS substitution already forbidden by LD-281.
(9) No session replay of kid-facing screens (COPPA landmine per Services Landscape Agent 4 scan).
(10) No ads/attribution SDKs in child app (AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch, Kidoz, SuperAwesome AwesomeAds, AdMob).
(11) No dragon avatar toggle (per ARC_5_DRAGONSHELL_STAYS_V1 — ceremony + patrol album kept, toggle cut).
(12) No Talk-to-Pip chat screen (cut per V1_SCOPE_CONDENSED_20260420).

These prevent re-litigation per session and protect clinical integrity from game-mechanic creep.

decision_name: All Phase B watercolor library tiles MUST be built via build_phase_b_tile.py (alpha unmixing + 2-matte frame)
decision_text:
Effective 2026-04-20. All tiles in Production/assets/watercolor_library/ MUST be produced via Production/Phase_B_Style_Guide/build_phase_b_tile.py. No hand-rolled background removal, no hand-rolled framing. PIPELINE: (1) AUTO-DETECT bg color from median of 8 corner/edge samples. (2) ALPHA UNMIXING (not masking): solve composite=bg*(1-a)+subject*a per pixel to recover (subject_rgb, alpha) separately. Eliminates dark-halo artifacts at anti-aliased edges that hand-rolled masking leaves behind. Alpha boost 1.5x per LD 186. (3) Crop subject to bbox + scale to fit 1024x1536 with 40px padding. (4) Frame per LD 203: 14px brown border + 22px cream mat. Output 1096x1608. WHY: Kim iterated 7+ rounds on hands_rubbing tile (black letterbox source) because hand-rolled color-key left dark halo lines. 'please update the code so this doesnt happen again.' Fix is proper unmixing, not masking. Script enforces it. CLI: python3 Production/Phase_B_Style_Guide/build_phase_b_tile.py <src> <dst>

2026-04-20 addendum (after color-cast regression): if source is RGBA with meaningful alpha (min channel < 250), TRUST IT — do not run unmixing. Running unmixing on an already-alpha-correct source double-processes it (convert to RGB composites subject with black → unmixing tries to invert but ALPHA_BOOST * clamp loses precision → dimmed result). Check: `im.split()[3].getextrema()[0] < 250` → use as-is. Else → unmix with corner-detected bg.

decision_name: prod_visual_assets schema — 13 provenance fields added (stillgen Phase 0 followup)
decision_text:
Provenance fields added to `prod_visual_assets` (2026-04-21) per handoff §7 Phase 0 and Kim

`prod_visual_assets`. Phase 1 endpoint design depends on those fields existing.

**Fields added (13, all nullable except is_current):**

| Field | Type | Nullable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `character_id` | string | yes | null | Character this asset depicts (e.g., 'benson'). |
| `is_current` | boolean | no | true | Whether this is the current live version. |
| `superseded_by_id` | integer | yes | null | If is_current=false, FK to prod_visual_assets.id that supersedes it. |

| `parent_asset_id` | integer | yes | null | FK to parent asset for derived assets (crops etc.). |
| `sha256` | string | yes | null | SHA256 integrity check (handoff §7 counter-agent β). |
| `generated_at` | timestamp | yes | null | UTC timestamp from the generator. |
| `replicate_job_id` | string | yes | null | Replicate prediction id. |

**Migration script:** `Production/scripts/stillgen_schema_migration_20260421.py` (idempotent; re-run safely).

**Other 4 dup groups from pre-migration scan are peer candidates (parallel options B/C
pending Kim review) and correctly kept is_current=true — all are live candidates, not

**Q2 resolution (file_path vs filepath):** data-driven pick per Kim's rule. In

decision_name: Stillgen two-path split — BFL Kontext Pro (masters) + Replicate FLUX 2 Pro (batch/delivery)
decision_text:
Stillgen pipeline uses a TWO-PATH model split (locked 2026-04-21 per Phase 0 Q4 findings).

**Path A — MASTERS (2048×2048 PNG): BFL FLUX Kontext Pro**
- API: `https://api.bfl.ai/v1/flux-kontext-pro`
- Produces 2048×2048 masters natively (per existing Rule 6.1 cropper workflow).
- Cost: ~$0.08/image.
- Used when: hero character masters, narrative still masters, anything that enters the
  master-cropper workflow (`/masters/` subdirs of Production/Event_N/ or Character_Assets/).
- All `role='master'` writes to `prod_visual_assets` go through this path.

**Path B — BATCH / DELIVERY-TIER: Replicate FLUX 2 Pro**
- API: `https://api.replicate.com/v1/models/black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro/predictions`
- 10-input schema (verified 2026-04-21 via schema introspection against latest_version):
  `seed, width, height, prompt, resolution, aspect_ratio, input_images, output_format,
  output_quality, safety_tolerance`.
- **Default resolution: "1 MP"** → produces 1008×1008 output. The `width`/`height` params
  are silently overridden by `resolution` when the latter is set; explicit `width: 2048,
  height: 2048` without bumping `resolution` still produced 1008×1008 in the empirical
  2026-04-21 test (prediction id `0snpggma2drmt0cxp69sd96szc`).
- For near-2048 output, set `resolution: "4 MP"` (produces ~2016×2016 at 1:1 — within 1.5%
  of 2048 target but NOT exact). For exact 2048×2048, use Path A instead.
- Used when: delivery-tier WebP (Rule 6.2) — ≤1280 long-edge anyway, so 1008 source is fine;
  batch character-variant expansion from a hero reference (the handoff §7 use case);
  non-Rule-6 iteration shots.
- Cost: ~$0.03-0.08/image (1 MP); higher for 4 MP.
- Supports up to 8 `input_images` reference images natively.

**What NOT to do:**
- Do not use Replicate FLUX 2 Pro for new masters — resolution mismatch vs Rule 6.
- Do not use BFL Kontext Pro for bulk cheap batch runs — cost scales faster than Replicate.
- Do not add a 1008→2048 upscaling step to the pipeline. Upscaling adds latency + detail
  hallucination. Use Path A when 2048 is needed.

**Output format:**
- Path A: PNG (baseline) → existing resize_to_delivery.py converts to WebP for delivery.
- Path B: `output_format` defaults to "webp"; set "png" for pipelines that expect PNG.
  Color type RGB (no alpha) — for character cutouts needing alpha, use Path A or a separate
  matting step.

**Provenance writing:** both paths write to `prod_visual_assets` with the new 13 provenance
fields (see LD STILLGEN_SCHEMA_MIGRATION_V1). `generated_by` = `'bfl:flux-kontext-pro'`
(Path A) or `'replicate:flux-2-pro'` (Path B). `flux_model` distinguishes variants when the
pipeline evolves. `replicate_job_id` populated for Path B.

**Test evidence:**
- Path B 1 MP test 2026-04-21: prediction `8ect0n0ax5rmr0cxp1fry5rfw0`, 10.4s, 1008×1008
  PNG RGB 2.04 MB. Succeeded.
- Path B width/height=2048 override test 2026-04-21: prediction `0snpggma2drmt0cxp69sd96szc`,
  11.4s, still 1008×1008 (resolution param dominates).

Related: preflight 140, task_id `stillgen-addon-phase0-resolutions-20260421`,
handoff §6+§7 + `STILLGEN_PHASE0_FINDINGS_20260421.md`.
notes: BFL Kontext Pro for Rule 6 masters (2048×2048); Replicate FLUX 2 Pro for batch/delivery (1008×1008 default, 2016×2016 at resolution=4 MP, 10-input schema verified). Do not mix paths. Provenance fields wired to prod_visual_assets.

decision_name: V1 scope FREEZE — no further reversals until M1-M6 velocity data available
decision_text:
No further V1 scope reversals until M1-M6 modules complete and pipeline-velocity data
is available (projected late 2026-05 or 2026-06 depending on production cadence).

**Context:** Two V1 scope reversals executed in under 24 hours:
- 2026-04-20 evening: Arc 8 Hopegrove UN-CUT (LD-332 revised first time) —
  `SCOPE_REVERSAL_ARC8_BACK_20260420.md`.
- 2026-04-21: Benson UN-CUT at M3 + Courage Stone un-fused + Oliver demoted
  (LD-335 superseded by LD-353; LD-332 revised second time) —
  `SCOPE_REVERSAL_BENSON_BACK_20260421.md`.

The second reversal was a logical consequence of the first (Arc 8 is Benson's
homeland — canonical Bible design). Phase 0 preflight 138 counter-agent C1 flagged
reversal-thrashing risk. Phase 0 preflight 140 counter-agent C1 flagged similar.
This LD operationalizes that mitigation.

**Freeze scope:** V1 creature roster, V1 arc list (9 arcs: Arcs 1-9), V1 stone structure
(6 domain + 1 Wisdom keystone, 7 total), V1 module count (54 = 9×6), V1 cadence default
(2×/week aspirational), V1 anti-patterns list (LD-344), the V1 tech stack (LD-343), and
V1 scope-defining LDs 332-346 + 352 + 353 + 354. The freeze does NOT apply to execution
details within that scope (storyboards, voice profiles, individual assets, module
ordering inside an arc, etc.) — those evolve continuously as production runs.

**Exceptions that would unlock the freeze:**
1. Kim-locked exception with explicit `SHORTCUT_*` LD per Rule 19 + written justification.
2. Pipeline-velocity data from M1-M6 lands and necessitates a cadence lock (LD-352
   supersession). That cadence lock is a NEW LD, not a reversal of existing scope.
3. A critical blocker surfaced during production that is actually IMPOSSIBLE to work
   around within the current scope — not just inconvenient.

**Enforcement:** Phase 0 classification for any proposed V1-scope reversal defaults to
ARCHITECTURAL (4+4 advocate/counter). The counter-agent must explicitly cite this LD and
argue why the reversal passes exception #1/#2/#3 above. If the synthesis can't clear that
bar, the preflight row MUST have `approved_to_proceed=false` and the reversal is blocked.

**Surface scope-pressure signals as blockers.** When calendar pressure, vendor delay, or
asset production difficulty suggests a V1 scope change, DO NOT propose the reversal
in-line — surface it as a `prod_blockers` row with severity proportional to impact, and
let Kim decide whether to unlock the freeze. The path of least resistance should be to
push harder on production velocity rather than to rewrite V1.

Related: preflights 137 (Arc 8), 138 (Benson), 140 (stillgen cascade). Handoffs
`SCOPE_REVERSAL_ARC8_BACK_20260420.md`, `SCOPE_REVERSAL_BENSON_BACK_20260421.md`. LDs
332 (revised x2), 335 (superseded), 352, 353, 354.

decision_name: CLAUDE.md Rule 24 â€” confidence annotation tags
decision_text: Claude MUST tag consequential outputs inline with [CONFIRMED against <source>] / [INFERRED - verify] / [GUESSED]. Applies to: numeric thresholds, named LD citations, counts, directive interpretations, math results from inference, mutation-scope assumptions. Does NOT apply to free-text prose, already-hedged language, Kim's own quoted words, or obviously present-context statements. Integration: mn-context SAVE harvests these tags into confidence_flagged_items[]; next CATCH_UP resurfaces them. Closes four failure classes: confidently-wrong synthesis, missing-the-question, counterfactual math, approval-gate bypass. Structural enforcement: none at ship; future may add post-response validator. Discipline rule per CLAUDE.md Rule 19 'no error paths' principle. Rule inserted in CLAUDE.md between Rule 23 and the Terminology Reference section.
notes: Rule 24 in CLAUDE.md. No structural enforcement at ship.

decision_name: CLAUDE.md Rule 25 â€” Kim-side [SCOPE: ...] tag convention (opt-in)
decision_text: Optional Kim-side directive prefix [SCOPE: ...]. When present, Claude reads the tag first, matches proposed actions against it, halts with one-line flag if action exceeds scope. Defined scope classes: file_edits_only, directus_read_only, single_file <path>, single_collection <name>, under_$<N>_reversible, doc_cascade_up_to_<N>_files, read_only. Expandable as patterns emerge. When tag absent: standing conservative-read behavior per Kim's 'flag in one line, don't halt' preference - no scope enforcement, no regression. Standing scope grants may be locked as LDs. Rationale: upstream fix for 'missing the question' + 'approval-gate bypass' failure classes. Zero friction when tag absent (opt-in only).
notes: Rule 25 in CLAUDE.md. Opt-in â€” Kim is NOT required to use the tag.

decision_name: post_item_verified() Directus write contract â€” read-back + deep-equality
decision_text: Production/lib/directus.py::post_item_verified(collection, payload, client=None) POSTs an item to Directus, reads it back by id, and performs deep-equality verification on every payload field. Raises SilentWriteFailure on any field mismatch, DirectusWriteError on HTTP POST failure, DirectusReadError on HTTP GET failure. Closes the 'silent partial write' failure class: Directus accepting a write with 201 but silently dropping fields (schema drift, permission-filtered, type coerced). Auto-fields (id, date_created, date_updated, user_created, user_updated, sort) are presence-verified only. int/float cross-type equality accepted (42 == 42.0). bool is NOT treated as int (strict). ISO-8601 datetime roundtrip normalized (sub-ms stripping, all-zero fractional stripped, UTC markers). Companion try_post_or_queue() provides offline-safe degradation: on write/read failure, queues to pending_directus_writes.json and never raises. mn-context SAVE uses try_post_or_queue for all writes. Tests: 20/20 pass (19 unit with mocks + 1 live integration against prod_activity_log). Callers: mn-context skill, all future session-start / session-end audit writes. Performance: +1 GET per write (~100-300ms); NOT suitable for tight loops.
notes: 20/20 tests pass (19 unit mocks + 1 live). Live integration writes to prod_activity_log confirmed id=1134 (smoke) and test runs.

decision_name: Phase A canonical auto-assembly pipeline (5 stages)
decision_text: Canonical Phase A auto-assembly pipeline locked 2026-04-21. Triggered by 'Mix Audio' button in storyboard panel. Stages: (a) ffmpeg extracts voice stem from raw lipsync video (phase_a_lipsync_<ts>.mp4). (b) ffmpeg amix combines voice (volume 1.0) + ambient bed (volume 0.15, normalize=0) into phase_a_mixed_<ts>.mp3. (c) ffmpeg -c:v copy re-muxes raw lipsync video with voice+bed audio → phase_a_lipsync_withbed_<ts>.mp4. (d) ffmpeg xfade concat flyin (3.8s) + raw-lipsync (10s) + flyout (2.3s) with transitions per PHASE_A_XFADE_RECIPE_V1_20260421. (e) ffmpeg overlay continuous ambient bed at volume 0.15 with normalize=0 across entire canonical duration (not just middle) per AMBIENT_BED_CONTINUOUS_OVERLAY_V1_20260421. Output: phase_a_canonical_<ts>.mp4 registered as role=delivery with parent_asset_id chain back to the raw lipsync master. Governed by LD-284 NORMALIZATION_BEFORE_CONCAT_V1 for codec spec (H.264 High / yuv420p / 1280x720 / 24fps / AAC 128 kbps mono 44.1 kHz / +faststart). Phase B is NOT covered by this pipeline yet — checkpoint notes 'Phase B still uses pre-produced audio+lipsync workflow'.

decision_name: Phase A xfade recipe: 0.5s fade in + 2.5s fadeblack fade out
decision_text: Phase A canonical transition recipe locked 2026-04-21: fade_in_s=0.5 with transition=fade (flyin → middle/raw-lipsync), fade_out_s=2.5 with transition=fadeblack (middle → flyout). fadeblack masks the unsynced 'Good luck!' mouth frames at the tail of the raw lipsync by dissolving through black at the fade midpoint — this is the fix for the 'open mouth at end' artifact that plain fade leaves visible. Iterated through 0.5 → 1.5 → 2.5 → 4.0 → back to 2.5 and fade → fadeblack; Kim approved 'good enough' at 2026-04-22 00:02. Values baked into the canonical assembly ffmpeg command chain in production_server.py. Any change to fade durations or transition type requires a new LD.

decision_name: Ambient bed plays continuously across entire Phase A canonical, not just middle
decision_text: Ambient bed overlay strategy locked 2026-04-21: the ambient bed must play continuously across the entire Phase A canonical (flyin + middle + flyout), not just the middle raw-lipsync section. Achieved by a stage-2 ffmpeg overlay: loop the ambient source with aloop, atrim to canonical duration, amix at volume=0.15 with normalize=0 against the concat'd video audio track. The middle section's bed (already present from the phase_a_lipsync_withbed re-mux) and the overlay bed double up acoustically but Kim's approval at volume 0.15 sounds correct — this is NOT a bug to fix. Do NOT attempt to remove the middle bed by reusing phase_a_lipsync_withbed_<ts>.mp4 in the concat; canonical concat uses the RAW lipsync for bit-exact ByteDance timing preservation. See feedback_canonical_uses_raw_not_withbed.md memory note.

decision_name: credentials.py skips URL-shaped values in API key parse
decision_text: Bug fix locked 2026-04-21. File: Production/tools/lib/credentials.py lines 89-95. Root cause: API_KEYS_MASTER.md contains multiple 'key' labels for WaveSpeed, including the hex API key AND the full Kling endpoint URL on adjacent lines. The legacy parser walked labels in order and let the later URL value overwrite the earlier hex key, so every WaveSpeed call went out with an endpoint URL in the Authorization header. Fix: the parser now skips any value that contains '/' or starts with 'api.' / 'http' / 'https' — URLs are never valid API keys. Verification: after patch, WaveSpeed auth succeeds on first call with the hex key; lipsync_sender.py dummy auth test confirmed HTTP 200 at the auth layer. Severity HIGH because the bug made every WaveSpeed job fail silently with wrong-credentials at the Bytedance/Kling endpoint, and because every new install of this codebase on a fresh machine would hit the same bug.

decision_name: lipsync_sender.py resolves WaveSpeed hostname via public DNS, passes IP via curl --resolve
decision_text: Bug fix locked 2026-04-21. File: Production/tools/lipsync_sender.py _resolve_host helper (lines ~270-330). Root cause: Kim's ISP (Altice/Optimum) DNS poisons api.wavespeed.ai to 167.206.37.145 instead of the correct 49.51.190.24 (Tencent Cloud). Any curl/requests call from Kim's Mac that uses the OS resolver hits the poisoned IP and either times out or returns garbage. Fix: _resolve_host() calls `dig @8.8.8.8` (Google) and `dig @1.1.1.1` (Cloudflare) via subprocess, picks the first non-bogus answer, and passes the resolved IP to curl via --resolve api.wavespeed.ai:443:<IP>. Verification: dig @8.8.8.8 api.wavespeed.ai returned 49.51.190.24; curl --resolve test with that IP returned HTTP 200 in 0.6s. Severity HIGH because ALL lipsync production is blocked for Kim without this fix, and the DNS poisoning is invisible (it looks like a WaveSpeed API failure, not a DNS failure).

decision_name: production_server.py lipsync handler uses LipSyncClient, not WaveSpeedClient
decision_text: Bug fix locked 2026-04-21. File: Production/tools/production_server.py line 7940. Root cause: the lipsync handler instantiated `self.app.client.submit_and_wait(...)` where `self.app.client` is a WaveSpeedClient (stills/motion client) which has no `submit_and_wait` method — that method lives on LipSyncClient. Call raised AttributeError at runtime, but the error hint ('try regenerating') obscured the actual class-mismatch. Fix: construct `LipSyncClient(self.app.client.api_key)` explicitly at the call site and invoke submit_and_wait on it (matching the pattern already used at production_server.py lines 4651 and 4824). Also rewrote the exception handler to include type(e).__name__ + str(e) in the user-facing hint so future class-mismatch errors surface cleanly. Severity HIGH because lipsync was the critical path for Phase A M1E1 and every call failed at runtime.

decision_name: ByteDance LipSync: max 10s per submission, no silence gaps
decision_text: RULE: Never submit more than ~10 seconds of video to ByteDance LipSync (api.wavespeed.ai/api/v3/bytedance/lipsync/audio-to-video). Never submit audio tracks that contain silence gaps. ROOT CAUSE 1 (scene hallucination): LatentSync was trained on 5-10s clips. Inputs beyond that range cause temporal drift and full-scene hallucination. A silence gap in the audio removes the audio-conditioning signal entirely, triggering visual hallucination mode where the model generates new content instead of preserving original frames. LatentSync uses a full-face mask (not just mouth), so hallucination affects the entire face region and can replace whole scenes. ROOT CAUSE 2 (Chinese watermark): China AI labeling law (effective 2025-09-01) requires ByteDance to stamp longer outputs. No API parameter disables it. Triggered above ~10-15s threshold. REQUIRED APPROACH: Split at silence boundaries. Submit ONLY speaking portions (each <=10s, no internal silence). For silent segments, passthrough original video frames without submitting to lipsync. Concatenate: lipsync_A + original_silence_passthrough + lipsync_B (if needed). Previous beats 01-11 worked because production server trimmed video to audio_duration+0.4s before submission. Always use production server lipsync path, never lipsync_sender directly for final production submissions.
source_document: Agent research: LatentSync GitHub #326, arXiv 2412.09262v2, China AI labeling law 2025-09-01

decision_name: Opus Model Escalation Protocol
decision_text: When Claude (Sonnet) detects any of 5 triggers it MUST spawn an Opus sub-agent: (1) second failed patch on same bug in same session; (2) cross-system architectural decision where error breaks a different system; (3) conflicting canonical authorities requiring reconciliation; (4) first API call to vendor not in API_KEYS_MASTER.md; (5) repeated frustration signal (keyword + same issue in prior Claude response — two-turn pattern). No per-session cap — escalate as many times as needed. Downgrade: return to Sonnet if Opus confirms task is routine. Supersedes LD-397 PHASE0_MODEL_TIERS_V1. Updated tier: Haiku=routine, Sonnet=orchestration+Phase0, Opus=escalated subtasks.

decision_name: Display Artifacts Must Be Re-derived from Disk, Not Ephemeral Memory Cache
decision_text: Any binary asset persisted to disk (PNG, MP4, WebP) MUST be displayable via a stable HTTP URL served from disk — NOT solely from an ephemeral in-memory JS cache (TH, blob URL map) wiped on page refresh or server restart. Pattern: (1) persist to disk at generation, (2) serve via static HTTP route with path-traversal protection, (3) render via URL; keep in-memory cache only for in-flight (not-yet-downloaded) assets. Root of: BG stills black-boxes after refresh (Fix C, 2026-04-25), Kling preview loss after refresh, Library Sidebar image loss (April 2026).

decision_name: Content Delivery Network Provider — V1
decision_text:
Firebase Storage (Google Cloud Storage via Firebase Admin SDK) is the V1 CDN for all module MP4 content. CloudFront was evaluated and rejected.

COST ANALYSIS (7 TB/year at LD-289 launch throttle — 2,000 families/week × arc-at-a-time delivery per LD-282):
- Firebase Storage: ~1.8 TB/year free egress (5 GB/day × 365); remaining ~5.2 TB × $0.12/GB = ~$624/year. Storage: 59 modules × 60 MB = ~3.5 GB at $0.026/GB/month = ~$1.10/year.
- CloudFront + S3: 7 TB × $0.085/GB = ~$595/year + S3 storage ~$1/year = ~$596/year.
- Delta: ~$29/year — not a material factor at V1 scale.

WHY FIREBASE STORAGE WINS:
1. Auth gating (COPPA): Firebase Security Rules + Firebase Auth provide content gating natively. CloudFront requires Lambda@Edge or a signing Cloud Function just to add auth — extra infrastructure with no other benefit.
2. App Check: Firebase Storage respects App Check enforcement natively (currently false everywhere per D1 item 7; will be enabled pre-launch per LD-345). CloudFront has no App Check integration.
3. D1 CF simplicity: Signed URLs generated via Admin SDK `bucket.file(path).getSignedUrl({action:'read', expires: Date.now() + 3600000})` — 2 lines. CloudFront requires managing CloudFront key pairs, private key storage in Secrets Manager, and custom policy construction.
4. Single SDK: Stream C download manager already uses Firebase Auth + Firestore patterns. Firebase Storage adds zero new SDK dependencies. CloudFront requires the AWS SDK.
5. US-only V1: No geographic distribution advantage for CloudFront at V1 scale. Firebase Storage on GCS is sufficient for US-only.

SIGNED URL AUTH PATTERN (all streams must implement):
- Module MP4s stored at: gs://{project}.appspot.com/modules/{arcId}/{moduleId}/module_v{version}.mp4
- Files are NEVER publicly readable — Storage Security Rules deny all public reads
- D1 Cloud Function `generateModuleDownloadUrl(moduleId, uid)` validates Firebase Auth token, checks arc unlock state in Firestore, returns a short-lived signed URL (1-hour expiry for large module download)
- Stream C download manager calls the CF with Firebase ID token → receives signed URL → passes to expo-file-system downloadAsync(). Auth is on the CF call, not an HTTP header on the Storage URL itself.

CROSS-STREAM IMPLICATIONS:
- D1: One Cloud Function required — `generateModuleDownloadUrl(moduleId)` (callable function). Auth: requires Firebase ID token in request context. Logic: verify auth → check arc unlock gate in Firestore → return getSignedUrl() result. URL expiry: 1 hour (covers large module downloads on slow connections). This CF is the only code that may call Firebase Admin Storage; no other service generates signed URLs.
- C: Download manager must call the `generateModuleDownloadUrl` CF (not a public URL), pass the result to expo-file-system, and NOT cache the signed URL beyond its expiry. Re-request a fresh signed URL on any retry after expiry-related 403.
- G: Firebase Storage egress monitored via Cloud Console billing alerts. Alert threshold: $50/month (flags unexpected traffic spike). Export Cloud Storage usage metrics to BigQuery for trend analysis. Budget line: ~$55/month at full 2K/week throttle.
- F: Upload script uses gsutil or Firebase Admin SDK. Upload path: gs://{project}.appspot.com/modules/{arcId}/{moduleId}/module_v{version}.mp4. Module version increments on re-upload (never overwrite in-flight). Checksum validation via gsutil -h Content-MD5 or Admin SDK metadata.md5Hash on upload confirmation.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE — CloudFront:
CloudFront cost is effectively identical (~$595/year vs ~$624/year). It loses on every operational dimension: requires AWS account + S3 bucket + CloudFront distribution + Lambda@Edge or signing CF, no App Check support, second SDK in Stream C, CloudFront key pair management in D1. The $29/year savings does not justify the operational overhead for a solo founder.

SUPERSEDES: No prior CDN LD. LD-404 MANIFEST_SCHEMA_V1 is pre-gate #0 (already locked); this is pre-gate #1 as named in SHIP_READINESS_PARALLEL_TRACKS_v2.md §Stream F item 2. Both gates must be locked before writing any Stream F upload script, D1 signed-URL CF, or Stream C download manager auth headers.

decision_name: Arc 2 Content Gate Before App Store Submission
decision_text: M2 (Luna), M3 (Benson), M4 (Ember), M5 (Bork), M6 (Bramble), and all Arc 2 modules (M7-M12) must reach listen_through status in prod_modules before App Store submission. Rationale: at 2x/week family cadence, fastest families complete Arc 1 (~6 modules) in ~3 weeks and immediately need Arc 2. Shipping without Arc 2 on CDN means the fastest families hit a dead end at week 3-6. This gate prevents launching a product that fails its most engaged users first. Enforcement: query prod_modules WHERE arc_id IN (1,2) AND current_stage=listen_through — count must equal 16 (6 Arc 1 + at minimum all Arc 2 modules) before App Store submission is authorized. Source: 2-Opus-agent completeness debate 2026-04-25, confirmed by both advocate and counter.

decision_name: Stream F Module Rollback Procedure
decision_text: Module rollback uses two paths implemented in upload_module.py rollback command. Path A (forward rollback): upload replacement MP4 as next version, atomically patch Firestore manifest (LD-404 fields), keep published=true — app detects contentHash change and re-downloads automatically (Stream C item 16). Path B (backward revert): revert Firestore pointer to an earlier GCS version — verify GCS object exists before touching Firestore. Both paths: --reason required for audit trail; arc_id inferred from Firestore; old versions NEVER deleted from GCS (LD-406 never-overwrite-in-flight). App cache invalidation mechanism: contentHash change detected by Stream C SHA-256 verify-on-read → stale cache deleted → re-download triggered automatically. Rollback audit fields added to modules/{moduleId} Firestore doc: rollback_from_version, rollback_reason, rollback_at.

decision_name: Arc Release Cadence Monitor V1
decision_text: ACTIVATION STATUS: INERT — cron not loaded; migration not applied. Activates when LAUNCH_DATE_V1 is locked in prod_locked_decisions. The schedule file (ARC_RELEASE_SCHEDULE.md) is a derived artifact. Planning anchor: 3x/week (fastest-family worst-case per LD-352: uncapped therapist prescription). Schedule uses relative offsets (T+N weeks from launch), not absolute dates. Slip-handling: no auto-cascade of downstream deadlines; slips surface as CRITICAL app_blockers and Kim re-runs the generator with an updated launch date. Arc 1 is bundled at install (LD-282) and is excluded from the schedule. CDN-live signal is Firestore arc_manifests/{arcId} (LD-406). prod_family_velocity_observations deferred to Stream F Item 8 (T+4wk post-launch).
