decision_name: Asset Findability Overhaul — Dropbox + Directus Convergence
decision_text:
[AMENDED 2026-04-26 by Kim feedback after initial lock]

Architectural decision: overhaul Dropbox + Directus asset organization to make every asset findable on first query — INCLUDING in-progress iterations not yet approved.

KIM'S CRITICAL REFINEMENT (added after initial agent debate):
The original 2-agent diagnosis optimized for the WRONG half of the problem. The 'find the approved one' case works fine because Kim says explicit phrases like 'Good enough!' that are easy to capture. The HARD case — the one that actually wastes time — is finding IN-PROGRESS iterations by their distinguishing features. Example phrases: 'remember that other one we did where the second half of the clip had better lipsyncing?' or 'the one where the magic trail was too aggressive but the first 2 seconds were perfect.' Approval tags + timestamps do NOT solve this.

REQUIRED ADDITION TO SCHEMA (extends original solution A):
- Add field `iteration_notes` (text, full-text indexed) to prod_assets — captures per-iteration distinguishing features in plain English
- Capture moment 1: at PRODUCTION time, Claude writes what it tried/changed ('regen with cfg_scale=0.5 + start-end frames; tail jitter remained')
- Capture moment 2: at FEEDBACK time, Claude captures Kim's verbatim feature comment ('second half lipsync clean, first half mouth drift')
- 'Find me X' protocol gets new step 0: full-text search iteration_notes for keywords from Kim's phrase. Returns matching rows regardless of approval status, sorted by timestamp.

KIM'S TIMING SIGNAL:
'Maybe a lot of this will be fixed naturally when we start working thru the storyboard.' Kim is uncertain whether to build the overhaul now vs. let storyboard work surface the real usage shape. AGREED — LD-421 stays as DIRECTION-ONLY lock. No schema migration, no hook deployment, no wrapper code until storyboard work creates actual demand. This is intentional Rule 19 + Rule 26 discipline against over-engineering before validated need.

ROOT CAUSES (verified 2026-04-26 via 2 parallel Opus diagnostic agents abb3e1999fb82f3c5 + a6b13ea0bf5b4e045):
1. Schema cannot represent approval — all 34 prod_assets rows status='pending'; verdict in unstructured notes (14/34). prod_visual_assets has supersession infrastructure but new skills write to dumb prod_assets.
2. 6.2% disk-to-Directus match rate in Event_1 (93/1503 unique basenames). Asymmetry proves problem is missing writes, not stale writes.
3. visible-magic skill = 0 REGISTER blocks; scene-to-production + elevenlabs-tts also dark. Compliance Gate (April 14) never applied to skills created after.
4. prod_activity_log.kim_verdict populated 26/1295 (2.0%); zero of 9 'approved' rows reference a filename. No FK from verdict to file.
5. Rule 31 has no enforcement surface — no PreToolUse hook on disk inspection.
6. Event_1 has 40+ subdirs, 199 files in kling_clips, 57 in preserved_winners (14+ tmp intermediates). Filenames encode ad-hoc reasoning + Unix epochs.
7. Sandboxed agent paths leaked into Directus (rows 70-71 of prod_visual_assets).
8. [ADDED] No structured iteration_notes field exists — in-progress iteration features cannot be queried, only the approval moment.

SOLUTION DIRECTION (locked but BUILD DEFERRED):
A. Schema additions to prod_assets: 13 fields (kim_verdict, kim_approved_at, kim_feedback, is_current, parent_asset_id, superseded_by_id, event_id, beat_id, colloquial_name, tags[], sha256, file_size_bytes, produced_by_skill) + iteration_notes (NEW per Kim refinement)
B. New prod_asset_aliases table for natural-language lookup
C. asset_id FK on prod_activity_log; activate prod_asset_versions + prod_approvals
D. Naming convention: {module}_{event}_{beat}_{type}_{descriptor}_{version}_{status}_{YYYYMMDD}.{ext}
E. Folder structure: Modules/M{N}_{Creature}/E{n}_{section}/{_winners,_intermediates,_rejects,stills/{masters,delivery},audio}/
F. registered_write.py wrapper + PreToolUse Hook A (block raw media writes)
G. Approval-phrase regex + asset_focus.json in-session tracking
H. 'Find me X' protocol: STEP 0 (NEW) iteration_notes full-text search → alias table → colloquial_name → tags → notes → STOP and ask. Hook B blocks disk inspection until protocol exhausts.
I. Migration: schema first → auto-backfill → Kim-marked TSV for orphans → archive
J. visible-magic skill into Compliance Gate immediately when work resumes

DEFERRED until storyboard work creates demand: all of the above. Direction is locked so when build time comes, no re-debate is needed — but no code/schema/hook ships preemptively.

EVIDENCE: 2 parallel Opus diagnostic agents 2026-04-26 + Kim refinement same day. Live Directus queries verified all numeric claims.

decision_name: Stitch Editor — Universal Video Assembly Tool
decision_text: The Stitch Editor is a standalone HTML tool served by production_server.py on port 5111 at /stitch_editor. It provides N-slot variable segment assembly with: per-slot ambient beds (volume control), timestamp-precise SFX cues (slot-relative offset_ms, drag-drop placement), between-slot transition sounds, a persistent sound library (ambient/sfx/transitions tabs backed by Production/assets/sound_library/), named job save/load (stitch_editor_state.json), inline browser preview via <video>, and LD-284-normalized bake with Directus registration via registered_write.py (module_id=1 sentinel for non-module-scoped outputs). HTML is produced by Rule 7 Path A builder (build_stitch_editor.py). All fetch() calls use absolute http://localhost:5111 URLs per Rule 32 (FETCH_ABSOLUTE_LOCALHOST_URLS_V1). SFX offsets are SLOT-RELATIVE (slot start = 0ms); server translates to absolute at mix time. Tool is universal — serves all future MindfulNest events, not hardcoded to Event 1. Finder drag uses file.path (Chrome only); Safari users use paste-path fallback input. Preview plays inline in the tool per Kim's JC1 answer. Finder drag path serving whitelisted to project root per JC2 answer. WaveSurfer 7.x CDN with __mnWaveSurferCDNFailed fallback; ws.load() only, never setMediaElement().

decision_name: zero-error-qa: Phase 1.5 + 6.5 — Boundary Contract Gates
decision_text: Two new BLOCKING phases added to zero-error-qa SKILL.md after post-mortem of Stitch Editor probe=1 bug (client called ?probe=1 expecting JSON; server returned raw MP4 bytes; QA passed because no gate cross-checked client→server contracts). Phase 1.5 Boundary Contract Manifest: for every fetch/HTTP/IPC call in the diff, produce a manifest row listing every query-param variant and expected response shape. Each variant must grep-match a callee branch — unmatched variant HARD STOPS Phase 2. Phase 6.5 Live Boundary Probe: after code is written, verify server start-time is AFTER handler mtime (Rule 29), then run a Python urllib probe for every manifest row asserting HTTP status + Content-Type + JSON key presence. Any probe failure HARD STOPS Phase 7. Failure class caught: client→server contract gaps where the variant is specced in the client but never implemented in the server handler. Root cause of the gap was that counter agents received prose summaries of handlers, not raw code — Phase 1.5 grep requirement forces handler code to be read verbatim. Decision rationale: 2-Opus-agent debate concluded both gates are non-redundant: manifest catches coverage gaps (spec time), probe catches behavior gaps (runtime, only gate whose input is not Claude's mental model).

decision_name: zero-error-qa Phase 7: Live execution proof required for all HTTP endpoints
decision_text: Static analysis (grep, code review, compile) is FORBIDDEN as sole proof for any HTTP endpoint, database write, or function that runs at user interaction time. Phase 7 verification table must show actual curl/Python urllib response output (status, Content-Type, response body) for every new or modified endpoint in the diff. Phase 6.5 probe stdout satisfies this requirement when copied into the Evidence column. 'No new endpoints in this diff' is a valid explicit declaration. Incident that created this rule: 2026-04-26 stitch editor build passed full Phase 0-7 QA with zero live endpoint calls. First user interaction revealed every functional API endpoint had bugs (wrong field names, missing import paths, missing query-param branches). The server returned HTTP 200 on the index route — which was the only live check in Phase 7. LD companion to ZERO_ERROR_QA_BOUNDARY_CONTRACT_V1 (Phase 1.5 + 6.5). Together these three rules close the 'Claude auditing Claude static loop' failure class.

decision_name: Content delivery: Cloudflare R2 replaces Firebase Storage
decision_text: MindfulNest module MP4s and assets are delivered via Cloudflare R2, not Firebase Storage. Firebase Storage egress is ~$0.12/GB; R2 egress is $0. At projected 7 TB/year scale, this saves ~$840/year. NOT Cloudflare Stream, Mux, or Bunny — those add transcoding/adaptive bitrate that pre-baked H.264 720p atomic MP4s do not need. R2 is object storage only; the pre-baked delivery model is a perfect fit. Implementation: upload_module.py writes to R2 bucket; CloudFront-style R2 public URL pattern in prod_assets.

decision_name: AI Parent Coach: Anthropic Managed Agents + Advisor Strategy
decision_text: The AI Parent Coach is built on Anthropic Managed Agents (launched April 8, 2026) as the foundation, replacing the planned manual parent_coach_cf.ts Cloud Function. Managed Agents provide stateful multi-turn context, persistent memory, tool calls, and crisis-detection hooks — all in Anthropic infra. The manual 60/30/10 Haiku/Sonnet/Opus routing layer is replaced by Advisor Strategy (beta header: anthropic-beta: advisor-tool-2026-03-01), which delivers Haiku-level cost with Opus-level quality on complex turns. Advisor Strategy is beta — build with a simple manual router as fallback. Architecture A (COPPA-only, template inputs, no HIPAA) is unchanged.

decision_name: zero-error-qa Phase 1.6 — Input Data Sanity Gate
decision_text:
Inserted new BLOCKING sub-phase Phase 1.6 (Input Data Sanity) into .claude/skills/zero-error-qa/SKILL.md between existing Phase 1.5 (Cross-Boundary Contract Manifest) and Phase 2 (Mechanical Execution). Catches the failure class where placeholder, corrupt, truncated, or under-sized files get passed to external generation APIs (gpt-image-1, Flux Kontext, Kling, Seedance, ElevenLabs, ByteDance LipSync) or media subprocesses (ffmpeg, ffprobe, imagemagick) — burning API budget on garbage and producing degraded outputs. SCREEN against malformed bytes, NOT a content guarantee.

Four checks (HARD STOP on any failure): (a) existence, (b) size floor [image >10KB, audio >5KB, video >100KB; NO floor for JSON], (c) format decode [PIL.verify for PNG/WebP, PIL.load for JPEG to catch JPEG truncation, ffprobe for audio/video — mutagen NOT used, ffprobe canonical per LD-284, json.load for JSON], (d) character-asset reference checks for paths matching 'Character_Assets/' directory or basename glob '*_master.<image-ext>' / '*_reference_master.<image-ext>': prod_assets registration check (sole exception to Rule 34 find_asset.py-first mandate, since this is path-equality verification not identity lookup) AND 256x256 dim floor.

Outcome classes: PASS / HARD STOP / DEFERRED (mid-diff generated paths — requires grep gate proving runtime helper is invoked) / PARTIAL (URL/base64/non-disk inputs — requires test -f check that runtime wrapper exists, else escalate to HARD STOP) / SKIP (trigger absent).

Helper script at Production/scripts/phase_1_6_input_sanity.py is callable from BOTH the QA gate AND runtime wrappers — single implementation, two enforcement points (closes static-vs-runtime gap surfaced by Phase 0 4+4 debate Counter 2 + Counter 4). Helper handles PASS/HARD_STOP only; SKILL.md governs DEFERRED/PARTIAL/SKIP.

Escape hatch: SHORTCUT_PHASE_1_6_FLOOR_OVERRIDE_{asset_id} decision per Rule 19 with explicit closure_date + status=active, queried at QA time; lapsed shortcut = HARD STOP.

Phase 0 architectural classification + 4+4 advocate/counter Opus debate ran at prod_preflight_reviews id=170 task_id=zero_error_qa_phase_1_6_20260427_165837. Synthesis applied 5 CRIT + 2 HIGH revisions. Cursor cross-review UNAVAILABLE in autonomous mode; substitute Opus reviewer + fresh Phase 3.5 counter agent applied equivalent rigor; both surfaced overlapping HIGH-severity findings (char-ref substring false-positive, existence-first ordering, DEFERRED grep-gate, PARTIAL wrapper-existence, SHORTCUT closure-date) — ALL fixed in v1.0.1 before lock. decision_name: build_gpt_still_prompt() rewrite required — _GPT_SPECIES_ANCHOR text overrides reference image
decision_text:
Production/tools/beat_generator.py:build_gpt_still_prompt() must be rewritten. The current implementation (lines 853-883) uses _GPT_SPECIES_ANCHOR (lines 715-740) to describe each creature in text — but those text descriptions contradict the actual reference images.

Concrete failure: _GPT_SPECIES_ANCHOR['Tessa'] = ('small green sea turtle', 'pale jade shell with darker edge plates, oversized round expressive eyes, short stubby limbs, no neck wrinkles') but tessa_shocked.png (the production reference) is a warm-orange-shelled cartoon turtle. The 1152-character prompt also includes 'Identity lock: this is Tessa, a small green sea turtle' AND 'Maintain EXACT proportions, colors, and facial features from the reference' — two contradictory instructions. Result: gpt-4o composites a green/jade hybrid that doesn't match the reference, even though it received the orange-shelled reference as an input_image block.

Empirical evidence: LD-431 Phase 6.8 produced 3 outputs (prod_assets ids 68, 69 via gpt-4o; id 70 via gpt-image-1) — all with the same prompt, all with character drift. 1. Remove _GPT_SPECIES_ANCHOR table (or repoint to descriptions that match the actual reference set).
2. Strip build_gpt_still_prompt to pose + emotion + scene-placement ONLY.
3. NO style dictation (no 'Pixar 3D', 'subsurface scattering', etc. — let the reference convey style).
4. NO character re-description (no species, color, anatomy text — let the reference convey identity).
5. Verify rewrite preserves bg_ref handling for beats where Kim has dragged a background.

Does NOT block other LD-431 follow-ups (LD-208 Doppler, _CREATURE_REFS DRY consolidation, etc.).

decision_name: Rive as preferred V1 fidget-zone runtime (CONDITIONAL)
decision_text:
Rive is the preferred V1 fidget-zone runtime. React Native Skia is removed from V1 child-facing fidget zones. Bubble Hop uses Rive state transitions for V1; Matter.js is a logic-layer fallback only if Rive bubble-on-bubble interaction feels insufficient on physical iPad 9. Decision is CONDITIONAL pending iPad 9 endurance gate (8 criteria — see §6.5.1). If gate fails, fallback to Lottie + Reanimated + bounded Matter.js for Bubble Hop only. No fidget-zone runtime ships unless repeated zone use does not poison the next therapeutic MP4 playback session. Rive avoids React Native Skia's specific risk class but is itself a native runtime — not a free pass; subject to its own mount/unmount, GPU memory, and integration testing. Supersedes LD-343's Skia inclusion in the V1 fidget stack pending gate result.

§6.5.1 LD-450 endurance gate (physical iPad 9, release build): Before the Rive runtime is locked for V1, ONE fidget zone (Star Window) must pass all 8 criteria below on a physical iPad 9 (A13, 3 GB RAM, 64 GB) with ~2 GB free RAM and the device running a release build. If Star Window passes, run the same gate on Glow Charge as a second confirmation (most Skia-dependent zone — biggest delta). If both pass, write LD-450 outcome=`passed` and migrate the remaining 3 zones. If any criterion fails on either zone, write LD-450 outcome=`failed` and proceed with the Lottie + Reanimated + bounded-Matter.js fallback.

Pass criteria (all 8 required):
1. Tap-to-feedback p95 ≤ 100 ms across 100 consecutive taps
2. No frame collapse under 5 minutes of continuous rapid tapping
3. Memory trend flat (within ±10%) across 20 mount/unmount cycles of the zone view
4. No crash after a 30-minute mixed session alternating zone → module → zone → module
5. Clean audio session handoff into Phase B meditation immediately after exiting the zone
6. Next module MP4 plays normally — Rive view does not poison subsequent expo-video session

decision_name: Event-load concurrency lock + monotonic generation counter
decision_text:
AppContext gains event_generation (monotonic int starting at 0) + event_load_lock (threading.Lock). New POST /api/event/load handler increments event_generation under lock and swaps app.event_dir / app.storyboard_path / app.event_id atomically; returns the new generation number to the client.

Concurrency contract: any handler that reads (event_dir, event_generation) reads them as a tuple under lock; any long-running async job pins pinned_generation at start (see ASYNC_JOB_GENERATION_PIN_V1).

Status code policy:
  * HTTP 423 (Locked) — async job's terminal write rejected because the event changed mid-flight. Client re-hydrates + retries once.
  * HTTP 409 (Conflict) — synchronous request's body event_id doesn't match server-pinned event. Client shows red banner + reload prompt (LD-456 SCOPE_VALIDATION_V1).

Single-user mode: Kim operates one tab at a time; lock contention is rare. Future multi-user: revisit lock granularity.

decision_name: Watercolor Animate — Workflow C (Claude API → ffmpeg filter_complex with safety gate). SUPERSEDES S4 magic_compositor approach.
decision_text:
Per Kim's S4-evening architectural correction: REPLACES the S4 implementation that called magic_compositor for watercolors. New approach: Claude API (claude-sonnet-4-6, ~$0.05/call) generates an ffmpeg filter_complex spec given watercolor PNG + manual_path geometry + motion_description text. Server validates the filter chain against a safe-filter allowlist BEFORE executing ffmpeg.

Allowlist (NO others): split, hflip, vflip, rotate, scale, overlay, blend, fade, crop, pad, drawbox, hue, eq, zoompan, fps, setpts, geq, displace.

Forbidden anywhere in spec: file://, http://, exec, system, run, backslash, pipe, backticks, $(…). duration_s must be in [0.5, 10].

On safety-gate rejection: HTTP 400 with {error: unsafe_filter_chain} + log Claude's response to activity log. On success: ffmpeg executes with 60s timeout, output mp4 written to watercolor_library/<key>_animated_<TS>.mp4, registered as watercolor_animation with parent_asset_id link.

Frontend: 'Animate this' on watercolor tiles opens path_picker.html ?mode=watercolor_animate. Picker has manual_path canvas + motion text field. After submission, animated mp4 appears alongside original PNG.

decision_name: @with_pin_and_drain decorator + drain endpoints fence migration windows
decision_text: Drain protocol: app.accept_new_jobs flag gates new sync work via @with_pin_and_drain decorator (returns HTTP 503 with code drain_in_progress when False). 14 sync handlers wrapped with track_sync=True (registers in app._sync_inflight set); 4 thread-spawning handlers wrapped with track_sync=False (drain gate only — their long work tracks via existing registries _GPT_JOBS / _MAGIC_JOBS / _ASSEMBLE_JOBS). 9 read-only/poll endpoints UNWRAPPED (must stay responsive during drain). New endpoints: POST /api/admin/drain_start, POST /api/admin/drain_end, GET /api/admin/inflight_count (full enumeration over all 5 registries + lipsync state-scan). decision_name: Beat Generator: 3 OPTIONS per beat (NOT 3×3 matrix, NOT 9 stills)
decision_text: Beat Generator UI MUST render exactly 3 GPT options per beat in a 1×3 row layout. There is exactly one character reference + one BG reference per beat; the backend submits 3 GPT calls (varied seed) → 3 options. NEVER a 3×3 matrix (9 cells of char×BG combinations), NEVER 9 stills, NEVER FLUX. Why: Kim explicitly cut the 9-stills approach 2026-05-02; agent memory had drifted toward '3×3 grid' phrasing. UI implementation must hard-cap optionsToShow.slice(0, 3). Spec ref: STORYBOARD_V59_S5_5_C_SPEC_v2.md §3.1 + memory entry project_beat_generator_3_options_not_grid.md.
